guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU/EEA social protection)

EE.note: Estonia's big instrument is time, not cash: 605 days of parental benefit at 100% of each parent's previous pay, usable flexibly until the child is 3, with a guaranteed municipal kindergarten place from 18 months. Universal child allowance is modest (€80/child) and the child-specific income-tax exemption was abolished from the 2024 tax year; there is no housing benefit reachable at median wage. Kindergarten fees are capped by law and Tallinn abolishes them for residents from September 2026; falling birth rates mean places are now generally available. On the wage side Estonia is simple and light: a flat 22% tax with a €700/month exemption for everyone from 2026 and almost no employee-side contributions, while the labour law adds state-paid child-leave days and 80% care leave for a sick child but no legal right to part-time work.

headline.cash: €160/month for 2 kids (child allowance €80 each) + €320 birth grant per child (2026)
headline.leave: 605 days at 100% of pay: 100 mother-only + 30 father-only + 475 shared, cap €3,806/month (2026)
headline.childcare: municipal place guaranteed from 18 months; fee capped at 20% of min. wage (€189/month), Tallinn free for residents from Sept 2026, food ≈ €4/day
headline.tax: none for children since tax year 2024; flat €700/month basic exemption per adult from 2026
headline.labourtax: flat 22% income tax; universal €700/month basic exemption from 2026 (≈ €1,850/yr per earner); employee-side contributions only 3.6%, social tax 33% is employer-paid
headline.workrights: 28 days paid leave + 12 holidays; 10 paid child-leave days per child per parent until 14; sick-child care leave at 80% from day 1

policies.name: Parental benefit (vanemahüvitis): maternity + paternity + shared
policies.what: Mother gets 100 days (up to 70 before birth), father 30 non-transferable days, plus 475 shared days parents split freely, all paid at 100% of previous average earnings (2026 floor €886, ceiling €3,806/month gross). Usable day-by-day until the child turns 3; up to 60 days both parents together; working while receiving does not reduce it.
policies.value: ≈ 100% of each parent's wage for about 20 months combined; at a ~€1,900 gross median wage roughly €38,000 gross per child
policies.eligibility: Residents; amount based on social tax paid in the 12-month reference period, minimum-wage floor if no income.
policies.caveat: Ceiling cut from 3x to 2x the average wage from 2026 (irrelevant at median pay). Employer must grant the matching leave; the 30 paternity days cannot be worked.

policies.name: Universal basic exemption of €700/month (maksuvaba tulu) from 2026
policies.what: From 1 January 2026 the income-tax-free amount is a flat €700/month (€8,400/year) for every working-age person, no longer phased out with income as in 2018–2025; income tax stays a flat 22% (the planned rise to 24% was cancelled). The employer applies it monthly on a one-line written request.
policies.value: ≈ €1,848/year less income tax per earner (€3,696 for two earners); roughly €1,400–1,500 more net per earner than under the 2025 phase-out rules at a ~€1,900 gross wage
policies.eligibility: All resident income-tax payers below pensionable age; apply once with the employer (only one employer may apply it).
policies.url_label: Estonian Tax and Customs Board — calculation of basic exemption
policies.caveat: No earned-income credit or child element: the child-specific extra exemption was abolished from tax year 2024. The exemption is not indexed.

policies.name: Child allowance (lapsetoetus) + childbirth allowance
policies.what: Universal, non-means-tested €80/month for the first and second child and €100/month from the third child, paid until age 19 (2026 rates). One-off childbirth allowance of €320 per child. Granted automatically after birth registration via the Social Insurance Board self-service portal.
policies.value: €160/month for 2 kids (€1,920/year) plus €640 one-off for two births
policies.eligibility: All permanent residents with children; no income test.
policies.caveat: Rates unchanged since 2023 and not indexed; the large-family allowance (€450/month) only starts at 3 children.

policies.name: Paid child leave (lapsepuhkus) + 80% care leave for a sick child
policies.what: Each employed parent gets 10 working days of child leave per child, usable any time until the end of the year the child turns 14 (max 30 days/year), paid by the Social Insurance Board at 50% of the parent's parental-benefit daily rate (floor €45.05/day from April 2026, cap €63.44/day). Separately, nursing a sick child under 12 is paid by the Health Insurance Fund at 80% from day 1 for up to 60 days per certificate.
policies.value: 2 kids: 20 paid child-leave days per parent (40 per household) ≈ €2,200–2,500 gross over the years, plus 80% pay on sick-child days; annual holiday is not reduced
policies.eligibility: Parents employed under an employment contract or in public service (child leave); anyone covered by health insurance (care leave, certificate from the child's doctor).
policies.caveat: Child leave cannot be taken while receiving parental benefit and only for working days; it is taxable. Care-leave benefit is 80% of last year's social-taxed income, not of the current wage.

policies.name: Employee-side social contributions of only 3.6% of gross pay
policies.what: Estonia's 33% social tax (pension + health) is paid entirely by the employer on top of gross pay. The employee's own wage deductions are just the 1.6% unemployment-insurance premium and the 2% default funded-pension contribution (optionally 4% or 6%), rates unchanged 2024–2026. Net pay is therefore gross minus 22% tax on income above €700 minus 3.6%.
policies.value: ≈ €68/month (€820/year) withheld per earner at a ~€1,900 gross wage, versus 10.5% in Latvia and 19.5% in Lithuania on the same wage
policies.eligibility: All employees; the funded-pension contribution is 0% for those who have opted out of the second pillar.
policies.url_label: Estonian Tax and Customs Board — tax rates 2024–2026
policies.caveat: This is a structural feature, not a family measure: the employer-paid social tax still forms part of total labour cost and holds gross wages down. No reduced rates for parents, overtime or bonuses.

policies.name: 28 calendar days paid annual holiday + 12 public holidays; €400/year tax-free employer health spend
policies.what: The Employment Contracts Act guarantees 28 calendar days (4 weeks) of paid annual holiday plus 12 public holidays (working days before New Year, Independence Day, Victory Day and Christmas Eve are 3 hours shorter). Child leave and paternity leave do not reduce the annual holiday. Employers may also pay up to €400 per employee per year for sport and health promotion free of fringe-benefit tax.
policies.value: ≈ 32 paid days off per year per parent; up to €400/year of tax-free sports/health spending if the employer offers it
policies.eligibility: All employees on an employment contract; the €400 health benefit is at the employer's discretion.
policies.url_label: Tööelu (Labour Inspectorate portal) — types of holidays
policies.caveat: No statutory right to part-time or remote work while children are small beyond the EU-minimum right to request; parents can only refuse overtime and business trips while raising a child under 3. Sick pay for the parent's own illness starts only on day 4 (70%, employer days 4–8).

policies.name: Municipal kindergarten place from 18 months, fee capped by law
policies.what: Municipalities must offer every child aged 1.5–7 a kindergarten place (from Sept 2025: an offer two months before the parent returns to work). Parent fee is capped at 20% of the national minimum wage per child (€189.20/month from Sept 2026). Tallinn charged €50/month and abolishes the fee for registered residents from 1 Sept 2026; parents still pay food (≈ €2.80–4.01/day in Tallinn).
policies.value: Tallinn: ≈ €80/month per child for food only from Sept 2026; elsewhere fee + food typically well under €250/month
policies.eligibility: Children registered in the municipality; Tallinn exemption needs child and one parent registered in Tallinn.
policies.caveat: Fees outside Tallinn are set locally up to the cap. Preferred kindergartens still fill up; Tallinn scrapped waiting lists in 2026 and now assigns places automatically, sometimes at a different site than requested.

policies.name: Free child health care, dental care and school lunch
policies.what: All children under 19 are covered by the Health Insurance Fund regardless of parents' status; dental care is free until 19 at contracted dentists. General education is free including textbooks, and the state funds a hot school lunch (€1/day, topped up by municipalities so most schools charge parents nothing).
policies.value: ≈ €0 out of pocket for GP, hospital, dental and school lunches for both children
policies.eligibility: All children resident in Estonia.
policies.caveat: Only dentists with a Health Insurance Fund contract are free; prescription co-payments still apply.

official.label: Sotsiaalkindlustusamet — overview of family benefits

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Estonia

ES.note: Spain has no universal child benefit: the only regular cash for kids at a median wage is the refundable mother's tax credit for under-3s. The real strengths are parental leave (19 fully-paid weeks for EACH parent since 2025/26) and free public preschool from age 3. Public 0-3 places are free in a growing number of regions (Galicia, Asturias, Madrid, Valencia, Canarias) but scarce; rent support for under-35s exists on paper but is income-capped and chronically oversubscribed. Spain takes little from wages in employee contributions (6.5%) and gives strong conciliation rights (adaptación and reducción de jornada until the child is 12, accumulable nursing leave), but there is no earned-income tax credit at a median wage and state tax brackets have not been indexed since 2015, so wage rises are silently taxed harder.

headline.cash: no universal child benefit; €100/month per child under 3 via the refundable maternity tax credit (+ up to €1,000/yr childcare top-up)
headline.leave: 19 weeks at 100% for EACH parent (17 + 2 flexible weeks, 2026); non-transferable
headline.childcare: free public preschool 3–6 nationwide; 0–3 free in several regions, otherwise income-scaled municipal fees; places scarce
headline.tax: mínimo por descendientes: €2,400/€2,700 per child + €2,800 extra per child under 3 kept tax-free
headline.labourtax: employee social contributions only 6.5% (2026); flat €2,000 work-expense deduction; no earned-income credit above €18,276; state brackets frozen since 2015
headline.workrights: 30 calendar days leave + 14 holidays; right to adapt or cut hours (1/8–1/2) until child turns 12; 1 h/day nursing leave accumulable

policies.name: Prestación por nacimiento y cuidado de menor (birth and childcare leave)
policies.what: Each parent gets 19 weeks paid at 100% of their contribution base (Royal Decree-law 9/2025): 6 weeks compulsory right after birth, 11 flexible weeks until the child turns 1, plus 2 extra weeks usable until age 8 (in force from 1 Jan 2026 for births since 2 Aug 2024). Not transferable; single parents get 32 weeks.
policies.value: ≈ 38 weeks of household income fully replaced per birth (two median earners); benefit is tax-exempt
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed registered with Social Security with a short minimum contribution record (none under 21; 90 days in last 7 years for ages 21–26).
policies.url_label: Seguridad Social — Prestación por nacimiento y cuidado de menor
policies.caveat: Payment capped at the maximum contribution base (≈ €4,900–5,100/month gross, 2025/26). A further 8-week 'permiso parental' until age 8 exists but is UNPAID.

policies.name: Free public preschool 3–6 (segundo ciclo de Educación Infantil) + regional free 0–3
policies.what: From the September after the child turns 3, a place in a public or state-funded (concertado) preschool is free of tuition nationwide (enrolment ~97%). For 0–3, public places are free in Galicia, Asturias, Madrid, Comunitat Valenciana and Canarias and partly in Andalucía; elsewhere municipal 'escuelas infantiles' charge income-scaled fees, typically €100–350/month.
policies.value: ≈ €3,000–6,000/yr saved per child once free; 0–3 saving depends on region and on getting a place
policies.eligibility: All resident children; 3–6 is a universal entitlement. 0–3 admission is by points (income, siblings, work status) and capacity.
policies.url_label: Eurydice (EU) — Early childhood education and care in Spain
policies.caveat: There is no legal entitlement to a 0–3 place; public 0–3 coverage is ~40% of children and waiting lists are the norm in big cities. Lunch, extended hours and materials are charged even in 'free' centres.

policies.name: Deducción por maternidad + incremento por gastos de guardería
policies.what: Refundable tax credit of €1,200/yr (paid as €100/month in advance on request, form 140) for each child under 3 to a mother who is employed, self-employed or on unemployment benefit. Plus up to €1,000/yr extra per child for fees paid to a licensed nursery (2025/26 rules).
policies.value: up to ≈ €4,400/yr for a newborn + toddler both under 3 if both attend a nursery; €2,400/yr without nursery
policies.eligibility: Mothers (or sole fathers) registered with Social Security; no income ceiling. Not combinable with the low-income child supplement (CAPI).
policies.caveat: The nursery top-up is limited to actual fees at an authorised centre and is claimed only in the annual return, not monthly.

policies.name: Vacaciones, festivos, permiso de lactancia y permisos familiares retribuidos (Estatuto de los Trabajadores)
policies.what: Minimum 30 calendar days (≈ 22 working days) paid leave plus 14 paid public holidays. Each parent gets a paid 1-hour daily nursing break until the child is 9 months, accumulable into ≈ 13–15 full days; 5 paid days for a relative's hospitalisation or serious illness and 4 paid days a year for urgent family reasons (since 2023).
policies.value: ≈ 36 paid days off per year per earner plus ≈ 3 extra paid weeks per parent per child in the first year; all employer-paid at 100%
policies.eligibility: All employees under the Estatuto de los Trabajadores; lactancia is an individual right of each parent (extendable to 12 months at reduced pay if both use it).
policies.url_label: BOE — Estatuto de los Trabajadores (consolidated text, arts. 37–38)
policies.caveat: Accumulating the nursing hour into full days depends on the collective agreement or an agreement with the employer; the 14 holidays include regional and local ones, so the exact calendar varies.

policies.name: Adaptación de jornada (art. 34.8 ET) and reducción de jornada por guarda legal (art. 37.6 ET)
policies.what: Parents of a child under 12 may request changes to the length, distribution or place of work (including remote); the employer must negotiate for 15 days and refuse only with written objective reasons. Separately, each parent has a RIGHT to cut daily hours by 1/8 to 1/2, with proportional pay cut, until the child turns 12, protected against dismissal.
policies.value: e.g. a 20% cut in hours costs ≈ €5,000/yr of a €25,000 salary but keeps the job, the seniority and (for the first 2 years) full pension credits
policies.eligibility: Employees with a child under 12 (no service or firm-size condition); the reduction is an individual right of each parent, the adaptation a right to request.
policies.url_label: BOE — Estatuto de los Trabajadores (arts. 34.8 and 37.6)
policies.caveat: Adaptation of hours is only a right to a reasoned answer, not to a yes; the reduction is unpaid, so only affordable where the household can lose part of one wage.

policies.name: Low employee social contributions (6.5%) and flat €2,000 work-expense deduction
policies.what: Employees pay 4.70% common contingencies + 1.55% unemployment + 0.10% training + 0.15% MEI = 6.5% of gross pay in 2026 (employers ≈ 30%), on a base capped at €5,101.20/month. In income tax every employee deducts a flat €2,000 'otros gastos' plus the €5,550 personal minimum; the up-to-€7,302 work-income reduction applies only below €19,747.50.
policies.value: ≈ €1,650/yr of social contributions on a €25,000 wage (versus €3,000–5,000 in most EU countries); the €2,000 deduction saves ≈ €480–600/yr per earner
policies.eligibility: All employees in the Régimen General; the deduction and personal minimum are automatic in the annual return.
policies.url_label: Seguridad Social — Bases y tipos de cotización 2026
policies.caveat: There is no earned-income tax credit for median earners: the new 2025 'deducción por obtención de rendimientos del trabajo' (€340) stops at €18,276 of gross wages, and the state brackets (€12,450 / €20,200 / €35,200) have not been indexed since 2015, so inflation-driven pay rises push more income into the 24% and 30% bands.

policies.name: Mínimo por descendientes (child allowance in income tax)
policies.what: Part of income is shielded from tax per child: €2,400 (1st), €2,700 (2nd), €4,000 (3rd), €4,500 (4th+), plus €2,800 extra for every child under 3 (2025/26). Split between both parents. Joint filing gives an extra €3,400 reduction, useful only if one parent earns little.
policies.value: ≈ €2,000–2,600/yr less income tax for two median earners with two children under 3 (€10,700 shielded at a 19–24% marginal rate)
policies.eligibility: Children under 25 living with the taxpayer with income below €8,000.
policies.caveat: It reduces tax, so it is worth less to low earners; the €2,800 under-3 supplement disappears at the third birthday.

policies.name: Bono Alquiler Joven (young tenants' rent bonus)
policies.what: Monthly rent subsidy for tenants aged 18–35: €250/month for up to 2 years under the 2022–25 programme, rising to up to €300/month (or €200 for a room) in the State Housing Plan 2026–2030. Applicant income must not exceed 3× IPREM (≈ €25,200/yr gross, 2026); rent caps of roughly €600–900/month set by each region.
policies.value: ≈ €3,000–3,600/yr if you get it; most two-earner couples are close to or above the income cap
policies.eligibility: 18–35, legal residents, rental contract for main home, income ≤ 3× IPREM; applications run by the regions.
policies.url_label: Ministerio de Vivienda — Bono Alquiler Joven
policies.caveat: Funds are limited and calls in most regions closed within days or weeks in 2022–2025 with long backlogs; several regions had not opened the 2026 call by mid-2026.

official.label: Seguridad Social — family benefits portal (prestaciones.seg-social.es)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Spain

FI.note: Finland gives a two-earner couple a long, gender-equal paid leave (160 weekdays each plus 40 pregnancy days), a legal right to municipal daycare at a low income-tested fee, and a home-care allowance if one parent stays home until age 3. Cash benefits are the weak side: the child benefit index is frozen 2024–2027 and general housing allowance was cut in 2024 and is unreachable at two median wages; there is no family taxation. Wages are lower than in the other Nordics, but the neuvola clinics, free child healthcare and free school meals are reliable and universal. Finnish wages carry ≈ 9% employee pension and unemployment contributions on top of income tax, but the earned-income credit (now with a 105 € per-child increment) returns ≈ 3,400 € per earner, and the law lets either parent work a 30-hour week until the child finishes second grade, topped up by Kela's flexible care allowance while the child is under 3.

headline.cash: ≈ 252 €/month lapsilisä for two under-3s (frozen until 2027); + 377.68 €/month home-care allowance if a parent stays home until age 3
headline.leave: 40 pregnancy days + 160 weekdays per parent (63 transferable) at ≈ 70% of wage; ≈ 14 months paid in total
headline.childcare: legal right to daycare from end of leave; income-tested fee, ≈ 180 €/month for two children at two median wages (max 335 + 134 € from Aug 2026)
headline.tax: none: individual taxation, no child tax credit
headline.labourtax: työtulovähennys (earned-income credit) max 3,430 € + 105 €/child in 2026: ≈ 3,400 € less tax per earner; employee pension/unemployment contributions ≈ 9% remain
headline.workrights: 5 weeks paid leave (30 days) + lomaraha 50% by agreement; legal right to 30-h week until child's 2nd school year; 4 sick-child days per illness

policies.name: Raskausraha + vanhempainraha (pregnancy and parental allowance)
policies.what: Since the 2022 reform: 40 weekdays of pregnancy allowance for the mother, then 160 weekdays of parental allowance per parent (paid 6 days/week, ≈ 6.4 months each), 63 of them transferable. Rate ≈ 70% of annual earnings up to 43,567 €, 40% above; minimum 31.99 €/day (2026). Usable until the child turns 2.
policies.value: ≈ 2,600 €/month before tax at a 3,800 € median wage; 360 paid weekdays per child (≈ 14 months) shared by the couple
policies.eligibility: Covered by Finnish social security; income-based rate needs earnings in the reference year, otherwise minimum.
policies.caveat: Employer pays full salary only if the collective agreement says so (often 1–3 months); untransferred days of a parent are lost.

policies.name: Varhaiskasvatus (municipal early childhood education) with income-tested fee
policies.what: Every child has a legal right to a full-time municipal daycare place once parental allowance ends (≈ 9 months). Fee is 10.7% of gross family income above a threshold (6,399 €/month for a 4-person family from 1 Aug 2026), max 335 €/month for the youngest child; second child 40% (max 134 €); free below the threshold. Pre-primary at 6 is free.
policies.value: ≈ 180 €/month for two full-time places at two median wages (≈ 7,600 € household income); at most 469 €/month
policies.eligibility: All resident children; fee depends on family size and gross income.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Education and Culture — ECEC client fees
policies.caveat: Big-city places can be far from home and staff shortages are common in Helsinki region; fee max rises from 311 € to 335 € on 1 Aug 2026.

policies.name: Työtulovähennys (earned-income tax credit) with child increment
policies.what: A credit deducted from income tax on wages: 18% of earned income up to a maximum of 3,430 € in 2026 (3,225 € in 2025), plus 105 € per dependent minor child (50 € in 2025; doubled for single parents), reduced by 2% of earned income above 35,000 €. Calculated automatically by the Tax Administration; higher maximum (4,630 €) from age 65.
policies.value: ≈ 3,400 € less tax per earner at a 3,800 € monthly wage (45,600 €/year) with two children, ≈ 6,800 € per household per year
policies.eligibility: Everyone with wage or business income; the child increment goes to each parent with dependent children under 18 (per child, both parents).
policies.url_label: Verohallinto — Verohallinto laskee nämä vähennykset automaattisesti (työtulovähennys)
policies.caveat: It cannot exceed the tax due and phases out with income; employee TyEL (7.15%) and unemployment (0.59%) contributions plus ≈ 8% municipal tax still apply.

policies.name: Lapsilisä (child benefit) + maternity grant
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, monthly until age 17: 94.88 € for the 1st child, 104.84 € for the 2nd, rising for further children, plus 26 € extra for each child under 3 (2026). Single parents get +73.30 €/child. Also a one-off maternity package or 170 € cash per birth. Index frozen 2024–2027.
policies.value: ≈ 252 €/month for a newborn + toddler; ≈ 200 €/month once both are 3+
policies.eligibility: All children resident in Finland; no income test.
policies.caveat: No inflation adjustment in 2024–2027 under the current government's savings package, a real-terms cut.

policies.name: Kotihoidon tuki (child home care allowance)
policies.what: If a child under 3 stays home after parental leave instead of municipal daycare, the family gets 377.68 €/month for that child plus 113.07 € per further under-3 sibling and 72.66 € per 3–6-year-old sibling (2026); an income-tested supplement (max 202.12 €) phases out by ≈ 4,258 €/month. Taxable. Parents working ≤ 30 h/week can get flexible care allowance instead.
policies.value: ≈ 491 €/month (taxable) if one parent stays home with the baby + toddler until the baby turns 3
policies.eligibility: Child under 3 not in municipal daycare; not payable for a child on whom parental allowance is paid.
policies.caveat: Some municipalities add a kuntalisä, many (incl. Helsinki) do not. From 1 Jan 2027 the government proposes restricting it to a parent who cares for the child personally and has 3 years' residence in Finland/EEA.

policies.name: Osittainen hoitovapaa (partial care leave) + Kela joustava hoitoraha
policies.what: Työsopimuslaki 4:4: an employee with 6 months' service may reduce working time to 30 h/week (typically 6 h/day) until the end of the child's second school year; the employer may refuse only for serious harm to production or service and must justify it in writing. Both parents may use it in turns. While the child is under 3, Kela pays joustava hoitoraha of 269.24 €/month (≤ 22.5 h/week) or 179.49 €/month (≤ 30 h/week).
policies.value: an enforceable 30-hour week for either parent for ≈ 8 years; + 179–269 €/month from Kela per parent while the youngest is under 3
policies.eligibility: Employees with at least 6 months' employment in the last 12; Kela allowance requires 1–30 h/week of work and a child under 3 (one child at a time).
policies.caveat: Pay falls in proportion to hours; only one parent can be on partial leave for the same child at the same time.

policies.name: Vuosiloma 30 days + lomaraha, tilapäinen hoitovapaa, employer sick pay
policies.what: Vuosilomalaki: 2.5 days per month = 30 days (5 weeks, Saturdays count) after the first year, with most collective agreements adding a 50% lomaraha (holiday bonus); ≈ 10 public holidays. Tilapäinen hoitovapaa: up to 4 working days per illness of a child under 10, paid in most agreements. Own illness: full pay for the day of falling ill + 9 weekdays by law, 4–8 weeks in most agreements.
policies.value: 5 weeks off + a bonus worth ≈ half a month's pay (≈ 1,900 € at median wage) per parent per year; paid sick-child days and full pay when ill
policies.eligibility: All employees; lomaraha and paid sick-child days depend on the (near-universal, generally binding) collective agreement.
policies.caveat: Lomaraha and sick-child pay are not in the law itself; the first year of employment earns only 2 days per month.

policies.name: Neuvola, free child healthcare and free school meals
policies.what: Maternity and child health clinics (neuvola) give free pregnancy care and ≈ 15 check-ups by age 6 plus all vaccinations. Public healthcare and dental care are free of client fees for under-18s. Pre-primary education (age 6) and school are free, including a daily hot meal.
policies.value: ≈ 0 € out of pocket for pregnancy, child health, dental and school
policies.eligibility: All residents.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health — child health clinics
policies.caveat: Wellbeing-services-county budgets are tight; waiting times for non-urgent care have grown since 2023.

official.label: Kela — Families (English)

guide.label: InfoFinland — Family (independent public guide)

FR.note: France front-loads support on the under-3s and makes school free from age 3, so this household's expensive years are short. Cash is modest but automatic (allocations familiales from the 2nd child, PAJE base allowance while a child is under 3), maternity pay is near-full, and from July 2026 each parent gets an extra 1-2 months of paid birth leave. The weak spots: a subsidised crèche place is far from guaranteed (roughly one collective place for every five under-3s, long municipal waiting lists), PreParE parental leave pays only about €460/month, and housing benefit (APL) is essentially out of reach at two median wages. Labour taxation itself is not eased for a median-wage couple beyond indexed brackets and tax-free overtime, but the non-cash side is strong: an enforceable right to part-time work until each child turns 3, five weeks' leave and near-universal tax-free meal and transport perks.

headline.cash: ≈ €350/month (allocations familiales €152 + PAJE base €198) while the baby is under 3, plus a €1,093 birth grant (2026)
headline.leave: 16 weeks maternity at ~full pay, 28 days paternity, plus new 1-2 months per parent at 70%/60% from July 2026
headline.childcare: école maternelle free and compulsory from age 3; crèche fee income-based (~€2.2/hour at median wage) but places scarce
headline.tax: quotient familial (2 kids = 3 parts, cap €1,807/half-part) + 50% tax credit on childcare costs up to €1,750/child/year
headline.labourtax: no earned-income credit; brackets indexed yearly; overtime pay exempt from income tax up to €7,500/yr and from 11.31% of employee contributions
headline.workrights: 5 weeks paid leave + 11 holidays; right to part-time (min 16 h) until child turns 3; €7.32/day meal vouchers and 50% of transit pass tax-free

policies.name: École maternelle (free from age 3) + income-based crèche fees (barème CNAF/PSU)
policies.what: Public nursery school is free and compulsory from age 3 (24 h/week, lunch extra, income-priced). Before 3, public/PSU crèches charge a national hourly fee: household monthly income x 0.0516% for 2 children, i.e. about €2.20/hour (min €0.41, max €4.39 in 2026-27), so roughly €350-450/month full time.
policies.value: ≈ €0 for the toddler in maternelle; ≈ €400/month for the baby in crèche (before 50% tax credit)
policies.eligibility: All residents; maternelle enrolment via the mairie; crèche places allocated by the commune, working parents prioritised.
policies.caveat: Crèche capacity is the catch: only about 1 collective place per 5 under-3s nationally, waiting lists of months. Fallback is a licensed childminder (assistante maternelle) subsidised via the CMG (complément libre choix du mode de garde, reformed Sept 2025), which costs a median family more than a crèche.

policies.name: Congé maternité, congé paternité and the new congé supplémentaire de naissance
policies.what: Maternity: 16 weeks paid by Sécurité sociale at net salary up to €104/day (2026), i.e. full pay at a median wage. Paternity: 3 days employer-paid + 25 days SS-paid. New from 1 July 2026: each parent gets 1-2 extra months at 70% of net salary the first month and 60% the second (salary counted up to €4,005/month).
policies.value: ≈ 4 months mother + 1 month father near-full pay, plus up to 4 extra months (2 each) at 60-70% for a median-wage couple
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed with recent contribution history; new birth leave open to both parents after maternity/paternity leave is used.
policies.caveat: Beyond this, PreParE parental leave pays only €459.70/month flat (6 months per parent for a first child; up to 24 months each for 2+ children), so long leave means a big income drop.

policies.name: Allocations familiales + PAJE (prime à la naissance, allocation de base)
policies.what: Allocations familiales start from the 2nd child: €152.25/month for 2 children at household income up to €79,980 (2026; halved above, quartered above €106,604). PAJE adds a €1,093 birth grant (2026) and a base allowance of €198.16/month until the child turns 3 (full rate for two-earner couples with 2 children up to €56,478 taxable income).
policies.value: ≈ €350/month while the baby is under 3 (€152 + €198) plus €1,093 at birth; ≈ €152/month afterwards
policies.eligibility: All legal residents; allocations familiales income-modulated but never zero; PAJE base means-tested at a ceiling above two median wages.
policies.caveat: Nothing for a first/only child under allocations familiales. Since March 2026 the age-14 supplement moved to age 18 for new beneficiaries. Rates only rose 0.8% in April 2026.

policies.name: Quotient familial + crédit d'impôt for childcare of under-6s
policies.what: Income tax is computed per 'part': a couple with 2 children has 3 parts instead of 2, capped at €1,807 of tax saving per extra half-part (2025 income, taxed 2026). Separately, 50% of crèche/childminder costs for under-6s is refunded as a tax credit on up to €3,500 of costs per child (max €1,750/child/year), even if no tax is due.
policies.value: ≈ €1,200-1,800/year from the quotient at two median wages + up to €1,750/year credit per child in paid care
policies.eligibility: All taxpayers; joint filing is automatic for married/PACS couples; the childcare credit needs receipts from a licensed carer or crèche.
policies.caveat: At a median wage the quotient saving is limited by the 11% bracket; the childcare credit excludes meals and any CAF subsidy already received.

policies.name: Congé parental d'éducation à temps partiel (right to part-time until age 3) + 5 weeks paid leave
policies.what: Any employee with 1 year's seniority can switch to part-time (minimum 16 h/week) after maternity/paternity leave until the child's 3rd birthday; the employer cannot refuse and must return the worker to the same or a similar job at equal pay. Statutory paid leave is 2.5 working days per month = 30 working days (5 weeks), plus 11 public holidays (only 1 May is compulsorily paid, but nearly all are off by agreement).
policies.value: ≈ 3 years of guaranteed part-time per child for either parent (income falls pro rata) + 5 weeks paid leave and ~11 holidays per earner
policies.eligibility: Employees with at least 1 year with the employer at the child's birth; leave renewable in 1-year blocks up to age 3 (longer for multiple births).
policies.url_label: service-public.gouv.fr — Congé parental d'éducation d'un salarié
policies.caveat: Part-time hours are unpaid beyond the flat PreParE allowance (~€260/month at half-time); statutory sick-child leave is only 3 unpaid days a year (5 if the child is under 1), and employer sick pay for the parent's own illness needs 1 year's seniority and starts after a 7-day waiting period.

policies.name: Titres-restaurant, 50% employer-paid transit pass and forfait mobilités durables
policies.what: Employer's share of a meal voucher is free of contributions and income tax up to €7.32 per working day (1 Jan 2026) when it covers 50-60% of the voucher. Employers must reimburse 50% of a public-transport season ticket, tax-free (up to 75% if they choose to pay more). Optional 'forfait mobilités durables' for cycling/car-pooling is tax-free up to €600/year (2026).
policies.value: ≈ €1,600/year per earner tax-free at the maximum voucher (≈ 220 days x €7.32) + ≈ €530/year in Paris (half of a Navigo pass) per commuter
policies.eligibility: Vouchers are at the employer's discretion (roughly a quarter of employees get them, more in large firms); transit reimbursement is compulsory for every employer.
policies.caveat: Small employers rarely offer vouchers; the €7.32 limit only applies if the employee pays 40-50% of the voucher; the transit refund needs a season ticket (single tickets excluded).

policies.name: Heures supplémentaires défiscalisées (tax- and contribution-free overtime)
policies.what: Since 2019, overtime pay is exempt from income tax up to €7,500 per year per person (ceiling raised from €5,000 in 2022 and now permanent) and from employee old-age contributions up to 11.31% of the overtime pay, applied directly on the payslip. Tax brackets are otherwise indexed to inflation each year (+1.8% for 2024 income, about +1% for 2025 income).
policies.value: ≈ €500-600/year per earner for about 100 overtime hours (≈ 2 h/week) at a median wage; €0 without overtime
policies.eligibility: All private-sector employees paid overtime (or 'jours de RTT' bought back); the exempt amount still counts for CSG/CRDS and for the revenu fiscal de référence.
policies.url_label: service-public.gouv.fr — Heures supplémentaires dans le secteur privé
policies.caveat: Only helps if overtime is available and compatible with childcare hours; France has no earned-income tax credit and employee contributions plus CSG take roughly 22% of gross pay at a median wage.

GB.note: For a two-earner renting family the UK's big instrument is now childcare: since September 2025 England funds 30 hours a week from 9 months until school for working parents, plus a 20% Tax-Free Childcare top-up, and Child Benefit is not income-tested until one parent earns £60,000. Everything else is weak: statutory maternity pay drops to a flat £194/week after six weeks, paternity leave is two weeks, there is no family tax relief, and Universal Credit (with its housing and childcare elements) is out of reach at two median wages (median full-time pay £39,039, ASHE April 2025). Figures are for England; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland run different childcare and school-meal schemes (see caveats). The 2024 cut in employee National Insurance is the only real relief on wages and is being eroded by frozen tax thresholds, while UK work rights give a generous 28 days' holiday and a day-one right to ask for flexible hours but no entitlement to reduce hours and only a flat £123/week if a parent falls ill.

headline.cash: £44.95/week ≈ £2,337/yr (≈ €2,700) Child Benefit for 2 kids (2026/27), no means test below £60k per parent
headline.leave: 39 weeks paid maternity: 6 weeks at 90% then £194.32/week; 2 weeks paternity at £194.32
headline.childcare: 30 funded hours/week from 9 months to school (38 weeks/yr) for working parents; +20% Tax-Free Childcare top-up
headline.tax: no family tax splitting or child tax credit; Tax-Free Childcare adds up to £2,000/child/yr
headline.labourtax: employee NICs cut from 12% to 8% in 2024 (≈ £1,060/yr per median earner); but personal allowance £12,570 and thresholds frozen until April 2031
headline.workrights: 5.6 weeks (28 days) paid holiday incl. bank holidays; day-one right to request flexible working; SSP £123.25/wk from day one since April 2026

policies.name: 30 hours funded childcare for working parents (England, 9 months to school age)
policies.what: Since 1 September 2025 eligible working parents in England get 30 hours a week of government-funded childcare for 38 weeks a year (can be stretched over 52) from the term after the child turns 9 months until they start school. Each parent must earn at least 16 hours a week at the National Living Wage (£2,643.68 per 3 months, ≈ £203/week) and neither may have adjusted net income over £100,000. All 3–4-year-olds get 15 hours regardless of work.
policies.value: ≈ 1,140 funded hours per child per year, worth roughly £7,000–£10,000 (≈ €8,000–11,500) per child at typical nursery fees
policies.eligibility: Both parents working and earning ≥ £2,643.68 per 3 months, each under £100,000 adjusted net income; reconfirm every 3 months via the childcare service.
policies.url_label: GOV.UK — Free childcare if you're working
policies.caveat: Providers may charge for meals, nappies and 'consumables' and for hours beyond 30; baby-room places are scarce in many areas; funding stops in school holidays unless stretched. Scotland (1,140 hours from age 3), Wales (Flying Start/Childcare Offer) and Northern Ireland (subsidy scheme) differ.

policies.name: Child Benefit
policies.what: Universal weekly benefit paid 4-weekly by HMRC: £27.05 for the eldest child and £17.90 for each additional child from 6 April 2026 (up 3.8%). Not means-tested unless one parent's adjusted net income exceeds £60,000; then the High Income Child Benefit Charge claws back 1% per £200, fully withdrawn at £80,000. Claiming also protects the carer's State Pension record.
policies.value: £44.95/week = £2,337/yr (≈ €2,700) for 2 children
policies.eligibility: Anyone responsible for a child under 16 (or under 20 in education) living in the UK; charge applies only if either parent earns over £60,000.
policies.caveat: The £60,000 test is per individual, not per household: two parents on £59,000 each keep it all, one on £80,000 loses it all. Rates are UK-wide.

policies.name: Employee National Insurance cut to 8% (2024)
policies.what: The main employee Class 1 NIC rate on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270 was cut from 12% to 10% in January 2024 and to 8% from 6 April 2024 (2% above the upper limit); rates unchanged for 2026/27. Income tax stays at 20% basic rate on £12,571–£50,270 with a £12,570 personal allowance.
policies.value: ≈ £1,060/yr (≈ €1,220) less NIC per earner on £39,039 median full-time pay, ≈ £2,100 (≈ €2,450) per household versus 2023 rules
policies.eligibility: All employees aged 16 to State Pension age earning above £242/week; applied automatically through PAYE, UK-wide.
policies.url_label: GOV.UK — National Insurance: how much you pay
policies.caveat: The personal allowance and NIC/tax thresholds have been frozen at £12,570/£50,270 since 2021 and the November 2025 Budget extended the freeze to April 2031, so wage growth steadily claws the gain back. Scotland sets its own income-tax bands (19–21% around median pay); NICs are UK-wide. No earned-income credit exists outside Universal Credit.

policies.name: Tax-Free Childcare
policies.what: For every £8 a working family pays into an online childcare account the government adds £2, up to £2,000 per child per year (£4,000 if disabled) for children under 12, spendable at any registered nursery, childminder, club or nanny. Works alongside the 30 funded hours to cover the remaining hours, extras and school-holiday care.
policies.value: up to £2,000/child/yr (≈ €2,300), i.e. up to £4,000 for 2 children
policies.eligibility: Same work and income test as the funded hours: each parent earns ≥ 16 hours at minimum wage and < £100,000; cannot be combined with Universal Credit childcare or childcare vouchers.
policies.caveat: You only get the full £2,000 if you spend £10,000 of your own money per child; eligibility must be reconfirmed every 3 months. UK-wide scheme.

policies.name: Statutory Maternity Pay, Paternity Pay and Shared Parental Leave
policies.what: Mothers can take 52 weeks' leave; Statutory Maternity Pay runs 39 weeks: 6 weeks at 90% of average earnings, then 33 weeks at £194.32/week (2026/27) or 90% if lower. Fathers get 2 weeks' paternity leave at £194.32 — a day-one right since 6 April 2026 under the Employment Rights Act 2025 (pay still needs 26 weeks' service). Parents may convert up to 50 weeks into Shared Parental Leave (37 paid weeks at the flat rate). Unpaid parental leave: 18 weeks per child.
policies.value: ≈ £10,500 (≈ €12,000) over 9 months for a mother on £39,000, i.e. ~36% of pay; ≈ £390 for the father's 2 weeks
policies.eligibility: Employees with 26 weeks' continuous service by the 15th week before the due date and earnings ≥ £129/week; self-employed mothers get Maternity Allowance instead.
policies.caveat: The flat rate is about a quarter of median full-time pay; employer top-ups are common in large firms but voluntary. Neonatal care leave (up to 12 weeks) added in April 2025.

policies.name: 5.6 weeks' paid holiday + day-one right to request flexible working, unpaid parental leave and time off for dependants
policies.what: All workers get 5.6 weeks (28 days for a 5-day week) of paid holiday, which may include the 8 English bank holidays. Since April 2024 every employee can make 2 flexible-working requests a year from day one (hours, days, pattern or home working); the employer must consult and decide within 2 months and may refuse only on 8 statutory business grounds, with a 'reasonableness' test due in 2027. From 6 April 2026 unpaid parental leave (18 weeks per child under 18, max 4 weeks a year) is also a day-one right; unpaid time off for a sick child in an emergency is a day-one right too.
policies.value: 28 paid days ≈ £4,200 (≈ €4,850) of paid time at £39,039; 4 weeks unpaid parental leave per child per year
policies.eligibility: Holiday: all workers incl. part-timers pro rata; flexible-working request and parental leave: employees from the first day; England and Wales (Scotland has 9 bank holidays, Northern Ireland 10).
policies.caveat: Flexible working is a right to ask, not a right to part-time hours as in Austria or Germany; employers can still refuse on business grounds. Parental leave is unpaid, so most families cannot afford it.

policies.name: Free NHS care for children + universal infant free school meals (England)
policies.what: All NHS treatment is free; prescriptions are free under 16, NHS dental care free under 18, eye tests free under 16, and the health-visitor programme covers checks to age 2.5. Every Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 pupil in an English state school gets a free lunch (Universal Infant Free School Meals); from September 2026 all children in Universal Credit households qualify at every age.
policies.value: ≈ £500/yr (≈ €575) per child in infant school in meals, plus no out-of-pocket child health costs
policies.eligibility: All children resident in the UK (NHS); all pupils in Reception–Year 2 in England (UIFSM); low-income families also get Healthy Start vouchers.
policies.url_label: GOV.UK — Universal infant free school meals 2026 to 2027
policies.caveat: Scotland and Wales give free primary-school meals to all ages; NHS dental capacity is poor in many areas even though the entitlement is free. No housing support exists at this income: Universal Credit's housing element is out of reach and the Lifetime ISA first-home bonus needs your own savings.

policies.name: Statutory Sick Pay from day one (Employment Rights Act 2025)
policies.what: From 6 April 2026 employers must pay Statutory Sick Pay from the first day of sickness (previously after 3 waiting days) and the £129/week earnings threshold was abolished; the rate is £123.25 a week or 80% of average weekly earnings if lower, for up to 28 weeks, taxed as wages.
policies.value: £123.25/wk (≈ €140) ≈ 16% of median full-time pay; the day-one change adds about £74 per sick spell for a full-time earner
policies.eligibility: All employees with a contract who are off sick for at least one day; employer-funded, UK-wide.
policies.caveat: SSP is a flat rate, not a share of salary: a parent on £750/week loses over 80% of pay while sick unless the employer offers occupational sick pay, which is voluntary.

GR.note: Greece pays a lot up front (a tiered birth grant, then 9 months of state-paid maternity leave at minimum wage) and has cut income tax for parents from 2026, but ongoing cash is thin: the means-tested A21 child benefit (equivalent income ≤ €15,000) is out of reach for two full-time median earners (≈ €32,000–35,000 gross combined). Childcare for under-4s depends on annual EU-funded vouchers and scarce municipal places; only public kindergarten from age 4 is free and guaranteed. Renting gets a modest new rent refund; wages are low and Athens rents high. Greece's biggest non-cash perk is the 30-month reduced-hours 'childcare leave' (a fully paid hour a day, worth roughly 3.75 months' salary per birth), while wage taxation has been eased mainly through 5.4 points of social-contribution cuts since 2019 and the 2026 family/young-worker tax scale rather than any earned-income credit.

headline.cash: birth grant €2,400 for the 1st child, €2,700 for the 2nd (2026); A21 child benefit only if one parent works less
headline.leave: 17 weeks maternity at ~full pay, then 9 months at minimum wage (€920/month); 14 days paternity; 2 paid months parental leave per parent
headline.childcare: ESPA voucher ≈ €2,000–2,800/yr per child for families under €35,000; free public kindergarten from age 4
headline.tax: 2026 family tax scale: 16% instead of 20% on €10–20k with 2 kids, credit €1,120; extra cut if a parent is under 30
headline.labourtax: employee EFKA contributions cut from 15.75% to 13.37% (2019–25, ≈ €400/yr per earner); overtime/night/Sunday premiums contribution-free since 2025; no earned-income credit
headline.workrights: paid hour off daily for 30 months after maternity leave; 20–25 days annual leave + ~12 holidays; flexible-work request until child turns 12

policies.name: Maternity leave + 9-month special maternity protection leave (DYPA) + paternity/parental leave
policies.what: Private-sector mothers get 17 weeks (119 days) maternity leave paid by EFKA plus a DYPA supplement so pay is roughly maintained, then up to 9 months 'special maternity protection leave' paid by DYPA at the statutory minimum wage (€920 gross/month from April 2026; extended from 6 to 9 months in 2023). Fathers: 14 working days paid paternity leave. Parental leave 4 months per parent, first 2 months paid by DYPA at minimum wage.
policies.value: ≈ €8,300 (9 × €920) per birth after ~4 months of near-full pay; + ≈ €1,840 per parent for 2 paid parental-leave months
policies.eligibility: Employees insured with EFKA (self-employed mothers covered since 2024); parental-leave pay needs 1 year with the employer.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Labour — 9-month special maternity leave (clarifications)
policies.caveat: The 9 months are paid at minimum wage, not salary; the father's 14 days are paid by the employer; public-sector rules differ. Applications run through the DYPA parental-benefits portal.

policies.name: Reduced-hours childcare leave (άδεια φροντίδας παιδιού) + paid family-emergency days
policies.what: For 30 months after maternity (or paternity) leave the employee may arrive 1 hour later or leave 1 hour earlier every day on full pay, or take 2 hours off for 12 months plus 1 hour for 6 more, or bundle the hours into whole days; either parent can use it. Also 4 paid days a year for school visits, 2 paid force-majeure days, and 8 unpaid sick-child days (2 children).
policies.value: ≈ 630 paid hours per child ≈ 3.75 months' salary (roughly €5,000 at a €17,000 wage), plus 6 paid family days a year
policies.eligibility: Private-sector employees after maternity/paternity leave (Law 4808/2021 and earlier collective agreements); the parents may share the hours but not both take them for the same child.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Labour — Employee leave entitlements (άδειες εργαζομένων)
policies.caveat: Taking the 9-month DYPA special maternity leave usually pushes the 30-month reduced-hours period to start afterwards; small employers may resist the whole-day bundling option, which needs their agreement.

policies.name: Birth grant (Επίδομα γέννησης, OPEKA)
policies.what: One-off grant for every child born in Greece, tiered since 1 January 2026: €2,400 for the first child, €2,700 for the second, €3,000 for the third, €3,500 for the fourth or later (was a flat €2,000 in 2020–2023, €2,400 in 2024–25). Paid in two equal instalments, the first the month after birth. Applied for by the mother online.
policies.value: €5,100 one-off for a first and a second child (2026 rates)
policies.eligibility: Equivalent family income ≤ €40,000/year; mother legally and permanently resident in Greece.
policies.caveat: The recurring A21 child benefit (€70/€42/€28 per child per month by equivalent income ≤ €6,000/€10,000/€15,000; scale 1 + 0.5 partner + 0.25 per child) is not payable at two median wages: €33,000 ÷ 2.0 = €16,500 equivalent income. If one parent goes part-time the family may drop into category C and get about €56/month for 2 kids.

policies.name: ESPA childcare vouchers (EETAA) + free public kindergarten from 4
policies.what: Each summer EETAA allocates EU co-funded vouchers ('Harmonisation of family and professional life') that cover fees at public or private infant-toddler centres for children from 2 months to 4 years; income limit for 2025/26 and 2026/27 is €35,000 gross for families with up to 2 children. Public kindergarten (nipiagogeio) is compulsory and free for two years from age 4.
policies.value: roughly €2,000–2,800/yr per child in fees covered (2026/27 call); €0 for kindergarten from age 4
policies.eligibility: Family income ≤ €35,000 (2 children); working, self-employed or job-seeking parents; ranked by points (income, single parent, disability).
policies.caveat: A dual-median-income family sits right at the €35,000 ceiling and low on the points list; municipal nurseries are oversubscribed in Athens and private fees often exceed the voucher. The exact voucher amounts change with each annual call.

policies.name: 2026 family income-tax scale + child tax credit
policies.what: From 1 January 2026 the rate on income of €10,001–20,000 is 20% with no children, 18% with one, 16% with two, 9% with three and 0% with four or more; on €20,001–30,000 it is 26/24/22/20/18%. The tax credit is €777 with no children, €900 with one and €1,120 with two. Workers under 25 pay 0% up to €20,000; those aged 26–30 pay 9% on €10,001–20,000.
policies.value: roughly €600/yr less tax per parent at €20,000 (≈ €1,200 per household); several hundred euros more if a parent is under 30
policies.eligibility: Every taxpayer with dependent children; the reduced rates and credits are applied per parent in the annual return.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Economy & Finance — Income taxation (2026 scale)
policies.caveat: Savings are small at Greek wage levels because most of the income sits in the 9% first bracket; the tax credit cannot turn negative, so a low earner gains little.

policies.name: Annual rent refund (Επιστροφή ενοικίου, AADE)
policies.what: Since November 2025 tenants get one month's rent back every November, paid automatically by the tax authority (AADE) from the rent declared in their tax return. Cap €800 for the main residence plus €50 per dependent child (€900 with 2 children). Income limits for the November 2026 payment: €35,000 for a couple plus €5,000 per child (€45,000 with 2 kids); property-wealth cap €120,000 plus €20,000 per family member.
policies.value: ≈ €900/yr (one month's rent, capped) for a renting couple with 2 children
policies.eligibility: Tenants whose lease is declared electronically to AADE and who file a tax return on time; income and property caps as above; nationwide.
policies.url_label: Ministry of National Economy & Finance (scheme owner; paid via AADE/myAADE)
policies.caveat: Regular housing benefit (Επίδομα στέγασης) is not reachable at median income. Regional public-sector doctors, nurses and teachers get two months instead of one. The state's 'Σπίτι μου II' cheap-mortgage scheme (ages 25–50) still needs a bank deposit.

policies.name: Employee social-contribution cuts (EFKA 2019–2025) + contribution-free overtime/night/Sunday premiums
policies.what: Total employee-plus-employer contributions were cut by 5.4 points between 2019 and 1 January 2025 (40.56% to 35.16%); the employee share fell from 15.75% to 13.37% of gross pay. Since 2025 contributions on overtime, night and Sunday/holiday work are calculated on the ordinary 8-hour rate, not on the 20–75% premium.
policies.value: ≈ €400/yr per earner (2.4 points on a €17,000 wage), ≈ €800 per household; a further ≈ €50–400/yr per earner if working overtime, nights or Sundays (ministry examples)
policies.eligibility: All privately employed workers insured with e-EFKA; the overtime rule covers full-time employees in every sector.
policies.caveat: No further cut is legislated for 2026; the 13.37% employee rate is still high relative to Greek wages, and the special solidarity levy was abolished for wages in 2021–23. Greece has no earned-income tax credit; the 2026 family and under-30 tax scale (listed under tax) is the main wage-tax relief.

policies.name: Statutory annual leave, flexible-work request for parents of under-12s, employer-paid sick leave
policies.what: 20 working days' paid leave in year one on a 5-day week, 21 in year two, 22 from year three, 25 after 10 years with the employer (12 years overall), plus about 12 public holidays. Parents of children up to 12 (6 months' service) may request telework, flexible hours or part-time; the employer must answer with reasons within 1 month (Law 4808/2021). Own illness: employer pays half pay for days 1–3, then full pay minus the EFKA sickness benefit for up to 15 days (under 1 year's service) or 1 month.
policies.value: ≈ 4–5 weeks paid leave + ~12 holidays (≈ €1,400–1,700 of paid time at €17,000/yr); 1 month employer-paid sick leave per year
policies.eligibility: All private-sector employees (leave accrues pro rata from day one); flexible-work request needs 6 months' service; sick pay needs 10 days' service.
policies.url_label: Ministry of Labour — Absence due to illness (employer's pay obligation)
policies.caveat: The flexible-work provision is only a right to ask: the employer can refuse with reasons, and there is no Elternteilzeit-style entitlement to cut hours. Part-time and undeclared overtime are common in Greek small firms.

HR.note: Since the March 2025 reform Croatia is strong on leave: about 14 months at full pay per child (maternity uncapped, parental capped at €3,000/month) plus 20 working days of paid paternity, a €618 birth grant and a real child tax allowance. Cash child allowance is means-tested below what a two-earner couple earns, so it does not reach this household. Childcare is municipal: cheap or free in Zagreb and many towns but with waiting lists and no legal entitlement to a place; housing support for renters is practically nil. Because the two parents are about 30, the 50% youth refund of income tax on wages is a real if expiring bonus (roughly €1,000 a year for the parent who does not claim the children), and working life is cushioned by sick-child leave paid by HZZO at 100% up to €995 a month and the option to take parental leave as half-time work until the child turns 8.

headline.cash: €618.02 one-off per newborn; monthly child allowance (€31-62/child) only if net income ≤ €618/household member
headline.leave: 6 months maternity at 100% uncapped + 8 months parental at 100% (cap €3,001.79/month), 2 months per parent non-transferable; 20 working days paternity at 100%
headline.childcare: municipal kindergarten: Zagreb most parents pay €0-40/month, elsewhere up to ~€170; no guaranteed place
headline.tax: monthly tax-free allowance +€300 (1st) +€420 (2nd child) → ≈ €1,700-2,000/year less income tax
headline.labourtax: income tax on wages refunded 100% until 25 and 50% until 30 (≈ €1,000/yr at a median wage); 20% pension contribution unchanged; no earned-income credit
headline.workrights: 4 weeks leave + 14 holidays; sick-child care under 7 at 100% (cap €995/month) from HZZO; parental leave usable as half-time work until child is 8

policies.name: Rodiljni i roditeljski dopust (maternity and parental leave)
policies.what: Maternity leave from 28 days before birth until the child is 6 months old at 100% of pay with no cap, paid by HZZO. Then parental leave of 8 months for a 1st or 2nd child (4 months per parent, 2 of them non-transferable) at 100% of pay capped at €3,001.79/month (680% of the budget base, since 1 March 2025; before that €995). Minimum €701.89/month.
policies.value: ≈ 14 months at full net pay per child for a parent on a median net wage of roughly €1,300 (cap of €3,001.79 is well above it)
policies.eligibility: Employed or self-employed parent with 12 months of continuous (or 18 of 24 months) health insurance; otherwise a flat €701.89/month.
policies.url_label: HZZO (Croatian Health Insurance Fund) — Rodiljne i roditeljske potpore
policies.caveat: The 2-month non-transferable father's share is lost if he does not use it; leave can be used until the child is 8 but at a lower flat rate after the first year.

policies.name: Uvećani osobni odbitak za djecu (child personal tax allowance)
policies.what: The basic tax-free monthly allowance of €600 is increased by €300 for the 1st child (coefficient 0.5), €420 for the 2nd (0.7) and €600 for the 3rd (1.0) (2025-2026). One parent claims each child, or parents split. Income tax rates are set by the municipality (about 20-23% lower rate in 2026, 30-33% above €5,000/month).
policies.value: ≈ €720/month extra tax-free income for 2 children → roughly €145-165/month (€1,700-2,000/year) more net pay at a median wage
policies.eligibility: Any resident taxpayer supporting a child whose own income is under €3,600/year; registered on the PK tax card via the employer.
policies.caveat: Only reduces tax actually due: a low-paid parent with a €600 basic allowance already pays little tax, so the higher earner should claim both children. No increase of the allowance in 2026.

policies.name: Očinski dopust (paternity leave)
policies.what: Fathers get 20 working days of paid paternity leave for one child (30 for twins) to be used in the first 6 months, at 100% of pay with no cap, funded from the state budget and paid by HZZO. Doubled from 10 days on 1 March 2025. Independent of the mother's leave.
policies.value: 4 fully paid weeks per child for the father, ≈ €1,300 net at a median wage, on top of his 2+ months of parental leave
policies.eligibility: Employed or self-employed father with health insurance; must be used within 6 months of birth.

policies.name: Porezna olakšica za mlade (income-tax refund for workers under 30)
policies.what: Since 2020 the annual income tax on employment income at the lower rate is reduced by 100% for employees up to 25 and by 50% for those aged 26-30, for the whole calendar year in which the age is reached (Income Tax Act art. 45). The refund is paid automatically after the tax year; in 2025 141,798 people aged 26-30 got back on average ≈ €958.
policies.value: ≈ €900-1,050/year (≈ €80-90/month) for a 30-year-old on a median gross wage of ≈ €1,700 who does not claim the child allowance; ≈ €0 for the parent who claims both children, whose tax is already near zero
policies.eligibility: Employees aged 30 or younger in the tax year with income from employment (plaća); paid via the annual tax settlement.
policies.url_label: Porezna uprava — godišnji obračun poreza na dohodak za građane (umanjenje za mlade)
policies.caveat: Ends after the year the parent turns 30; only reduces income tax, not the 20% pension contribution; worth little to a parent who already uses the child allowance.

policies.name: Jednokratna novčana potpora za novorođeno dijete (birth grant)
policies.what: One-off state payment of €618.02 per newborn (140% of the budget base), doubled from €309 on 1 March 2025, claimed from HZZO within 6 months of birth. Most cities and counties pay their own additional newborn grants (typically €300-1,300; Zagreb and coastal towns higher), and Zagreb co-finances private kindergartens.
policies.value: €1,236 from the state for two births, plus a municipal grant of a few hundred euros each in most towns
policies.eligibility: Croatian citizen or permanent resident with health insurance; no income test.
policies.url_label: gov.hr — Novčana potpora za novorođeno dijete
policies.caveat: The monthly child allowance (doplatak za djecu, €30.90-61.80 per child) is paid only if net income per household member is at most €618.02/month, so a two-median-wage couple with 2 children usually does not qualify.

policies.name: Sufinancirani gradski vrtići + besplatni školski obroci (subsidised municipal kindergarten, free school meals)
policies.what: Kindergartens (from 1 year) are run and priced by municipalities. In Zagreb the parent fee is income-based: about a third of parents pay €0-20/month and most under €40 against an economic price of ~€340; 17 towns charge nothing, others up to ~€170/month. The pre-school year is free. Since 2023/24 the state pays €1.33 per school meal for every primary-school pupil, and primary textbooks are state-funded.
policies.value: ≈ €0-80/month for a 3-year-old in a city kindergarten (Zagreb ≈ €0-40); free meals and textbooks once in primary school
policies.eligibility: Residence in the municipality; both parents employed usually gives priority; no legal entitlement to a place.
policies.caveat: Waiting lists in Zagreb, Split and the coast are long for under-3s; private kindergartens cost €300-500/month (Zagreb subsidises them by ~€400). Fees and capacity vary enormously by municipality.

policies.name: Naknada plaće za njegu djeteta i bolovanje (paid sick-child care and own sick pay)
policies.what: A parent kept off work to care for a sick child under 7 receives 100% of the pay base from HZZO from day 1, capped at €995.45 per month (2026); for own illness the employer pays the first 42 days at not less than 70% of the base (collective agreements often 85-100%), from day 43 HZZO pays at least 70% up to the same cap. Breastfeeding mothers get a paid 2-hour daily break until the child is 1, paid by HZZO.
policies.value: ≈ €995/month (≈ 77% of a €1,300 net median wage) while caring for a sick child under 7; own sick leave ≥ 70% (≈ €910/month) for the first 42 days
policies.eligibility: Insured employees with 9 months of continuous or 12 months of HZZO insurance in the last 2 years; doctor's certificate; sick-child care for a child under 7 (older children at lower rates).
policies.url_label: HZZO — naknada plaće za vrijeme privremene nesposobnosti za rad
policies.caveat: The €995.45 cap bites above ≈ €1,000 net; care of a child aged 7 or older is paid at 70%.

policies.name: Godišnji odmor, blagdani i rad s polovicom radnog vremena (leave, holidays, half-time work for parents)
policies.what: Labour Act: at least 4 weeks of paid annual leave (art. 77) plus 14 public holidays; a parent of a child under 3 cannot be ordered to work overtime without written consent (art. 65). Under the parental-benefits law, parental leave can be taken as half-time work until the child is 8 (twice the duration), and a parent may work half-time until the child is 3 if the child needs enhanced care.
policies.value: ≈ 34 paid days off per year per earner; up to 16 months of half-days for the second parent after the mother's leave, with HZZO topping up the unworked half
policies.eligibility: All employees (leave, overtime protection); half-time parental leave for employed parents who have unused parental leave.
policies.caveat: No general statutory right to part-time or remote work once parental leave is used up; part-time depends on the employer.

HU.note: Hungary channels most support through the tax system, which suits a dual-earner household: the doubled family tax allowance (80,000 HUF/month for two children) plus, from January 2026, a lifelong 0% income tax for mothers under 40 with two children, and tax-free earnings-related leave (CSED 100% for 6 months, GYED 70% to age 2). Flat cash benefits are weak — the universal családi pótlék has been frozen at 12,200–16,000 HUF per child since 2008. Kindergarten is free and guaranteed from age 3; crèche places for under-3s are uneven outside cities. Housing schemes (Otthon Start 3% loan, CSOK Plusz) need a 10% deposit or a mortgage; only the Babaváró loan is reachable without savings. Labour taxes are flat (15% PIT, 18.5% contributions) with no general work credit, but for this household the mother's wage is effectively income-tax-free — under 30 with one child since 2023, and for life with two children from 2026 — while work rights add a hard legal claim to half-time until each child turns 4, two to four extra leave days per parent and long paid sick-child allowances.

headline.cash: családi pótlék 26,600 HUF/month (≈ €67) for 2 kids, frozen since 2008; Babaváró 11m HUF (≈ €28k) interest-free loan, 30% forgiven at 2nd child
headline.leave: CSED 100% of pay for 24 weeks, then GYED 70% (cap 451,920 HUF/month, 2026) until age 2 — both tax-free; father may take GYED
headline.childcare: óvoda free and guaranteed from age 3 (compulsory); crèche fee ≤ 25% of per-capita income; free meals below ~279,000 HUF per-capita net income
headline.tax: family tax allowance 40,000 HUF per child per month with 2 kids (≈ €200/month) + 0% PIT for mothers of two under 40 from 2026
headline.labourtax: 15% flat PIT, 18.5% contributions; mothers of two pay 0% PIT from 2026 and mothers under 30 pay 0% on wages since 2023; no general earned-income credit
headline.workrights: 20 days + age and child extra days (26 for a 30-year-old with 2 kids) + 11 holidays; legal right to half-time until child turns 4; 15 sick days at 70%

policies.name: Családi (adó)kedvezmény — family tax allowance
policies.what: Reduces income tax by 20,000 HUF/month with one child, 40,000 HUF per child with two, 66,000 HUF per child with three or more (2026, after doubling in 2025–26). Any part not usable against the 15% PIT is deducted from the 18.5% social-security contribution. Parents may split it; counts from the 91st day of pregnancy.
policies.value: 80,000 HUF/month (≈ €200), i.e. ≈ 960,000 HUF/year, for two children — typically claimed by the father while the mother is PIT-exempt
policies.eligibility: Parents entitled to családi pótlék for the child (all residents); needs taxable earned income or contributions to offset.
policies.caveat: Worth the full amount only if the claiming parent's PIT + contributions reach 80,000 HUF/month (gross ≈ 240,000 HUF) — fine at a median wage, not while on GYES.

policies.name: CSED + GYED (earnings-related maternity and childcare benefit)
policies.what: CSED: 100% of average daily gross earnings for 168 days (24 weeks) from birth. GYED: from day 169 until the child's 2nd birthday, 70% of previous earnings, capped at 70% of twice the minimum wage — 451,920 HUF/month in 2026. Both PIT-exempt since July 2025, so net pay can exceed the previous salary. Father may take GYED; the parent may work without limit once the child is 6 months old. Then GYES 28,500 HUF/month to age 3.
policies.value: ≈ 520,000 HUF/month (≈ €1,300) tax-free for 6 months, then ≈ 365,000 HUF/month (≈ €920) for 18 months at a median wage
policies.eligibility: 365 days of insurance (employment) in the 2 years before birth; GYED also for the father.
policies.caveat: Uninsured parents get only the flat GYES (28,500 HUF/month); the GYED cap bites above ~645,000 HUF gross.

policies.name: Kétgyermekes anyák szja-mentessége — 0% income tax for mothers of two
policies.what: From 1 January 2026 mothers under 40 who raise (or raised for 12+ years) two children pay no personal income tax on any earned income — wages, self-employment, commissions — for life, with no cap. Phased in by age: under 40 in 2026, under 50 from 2027, under 60 from 2028, all from 2029. Claimed via a tax-advance declaration to the employer.
policies.value: ≈ 78,000 HUF/month (≈ €200), i.e. 15% of gross, for a mother on a median wage (~520,000 HUF)
policies.eligibility: Mothers with at least two children who are (or were for 12 years) entitled to családi pótlék; in 2026 only those born after 31 December 1985.
policies.caveat: Applies only to the mother's earned income (not capital or rental income); contributions (18.5%) are still due. Mothers of three or more have been exempt since 2019.

policies.name: Babaváró támogatás — 11 million HUF interest-free loan
policies.what: Unsecured bank loan of up to 11 million HUF (≈ €28,000) for married couples where the wife is aged 18–35, repayable over up to 20 years (max 51,000 HUF/month), interest-free if a child is born within 5 years. Repayment is suspended 3 years per child; 30% of the debt is written off at the second child and all of it at the third. Usable for a rental deposit, furnishing or a home purchase.
policies.value: ≈ 3.3 million HUF (≈ €8,400) forgiven with two children plus an interest-free 11m HUF loan (0.5%/year guarantee fee)
policies.eligibility: Married couple, wife 18–35, one spouse with 3 years of social insurance, clean credit record.
policies.caveat: If no child arrives within 5 years the loan becomes market-rate and the interest subsidy must be repaid. The 3% fixed Otthon Start mortgage (up to 50m HUF, from Sept 2025) is the main first-home scheme but needs a 10% deposit.

policies.name: 30 év alatti anyák kedvezménye — 0% income tax for mothers under 30 (uncapped from 2026)
policies.what: Since 1 January 2023 a woman whose entitlement to családi pótlék (child, or pregnancy from week 12) opens before her 30th birthday pays no personal income tax on wage and other earned income until the end of the year in which she turns 30. Until 2025 the exempt amount was capped at the previous July's national average gross wage; from 2026 the whole wage is exempt. Claimed via an advance-tax declaration to the employer.
policies.value: ≈ 78,000 HUF/month (≈ €195), i.e. 15% of a ~520,000 HUF median gross wage, for a mother aged 28–30 — ≈ 940,000 HUF/year until she turns 30, after which the mothers-of-two exemption can take over
policies.eligibility: Mothers (married, partnered or single) who have or expect their first child before age 30; from 2026 also uncapped; the family tax allowance can still be set against contributions.
policies.url_label: csalad.hu — SZJA 30: a 30 év alatti anyák szja-mentessége
policies.caveat: Ends with the year of the 30th birthday; a first child at 30 or later gives nothing unless a second follows (then 0% from 2026); the 18.5% contributions remain due; fathers get no equivalent.

policies.name: Legal right to half-time until the child turns 4 (Mt. 61. § (3)) + flexible-work request until 8, dismissal limits until 3
policies.what: On the employee's proposal the employer must amend the contract to part-time equal to half the full daily working time until the child is 4 (6 with three or more children) — no refusal possible. Until the child is 8 an employee may request remote work, part-time or a changed schedule and the employer must answer within 15 days with written reasons. Dismissal is banned during pregnancy, maternity leave and unpaid childcare leave, and until the child is 3 a mother (or single father) may be dismissed for capability or operational reasons only if no suitable other job is offered. Fathers get 10 working days of apasági szabadság (first 5 at 100%, next 5 at 40%). Nursing mothers get 2 × 1 hour paid daily until 6 months, 1 hour until 9 months.
policies.value: 20 hours a week by right for up to 4 years per child — 8 years back-to-back with two children born 2 years apart — at pro-rata pay, keeping the job and the family tax allowance
policies.eligibility: All employees under the Labour Code (Mt.), except during the first 6 months of employment for the flexible-work request; the half-time right has no tenure condition.
policies.url_label: Jogtár — 2012. évi I. törvény a munka törvénykönyvéről (Mt.) 61. §, 65–66. §, 118. §
policies.caveat: Half-time is exactly 50% — no right to 60–80%; the under-8 flexible request is only a right to a reasoned answer; the dismissal shield after leave is a procedural hurdle, not a ban; public-sector staff fall under separate acts.

policies.name: Paid leave 20 days + age days + 2/4 days per parent for children + 11 holidays; 15 sick days at 70%; long paid sick-child allowance
policies.what: Basic leave is 20 working days plus 1 day from age 25, 2 from 28, 3 from 31 (up to 10 at 45) plus, for each parent, 2 extra days with one child, 4 with two, 7 with three or more under 16; 11 public holidays. Own illness: the employer pays 15 days a year of betegszabadság at 70% of absence pay, then táppénz at 60% (50% with under 2 years' insurance). Sick child: táppénz per child per year without limit under age 1, 84 days at age 1–3, 42 days at 3–6 (168/84 for single parents), 14 days at 6–12.
policies.value: 26 days each (20 + 2 age + 4 child) + ~9 weekday holidays ≈ 7 weeks off at full pay per parent; up to 84 paid days a year at home with a sick toddler
policies.eligibility: All employees under the Mt.; táppénz needs current social insurance (automatic for employees); child extra days go to both parents.
policies.caveat: Táppénz is capped at twice the daily minimum wage (≈ 19,300 HUF/day in 2026) and paid at 60% or 50%, so a sick month costs ~40% of pay; Hungary's 11 public holidays are among the fewest in the EU.

policies.name: Free óvoda from age 3, subsidised bölcsőde, free meals
policies.what: Kindergarten (óvoda) is compulsory and free of charge from the September after the child turns 3, with a guaranteed place; only meals are charged. Crèches (bölcsőde, 0–3) may charge a care fee of at most 25% of per-capita net family income — many municipalities charge nothing. Meals in both are free for families with per-capita net income below 130% of the net minimum wage (≈ 279,000 HUF in 2026) or with 3+ children. Textbooks and child healthcare are free.
policies.value: Full-day kindergarten for roughly 0–15,000 HUF/month in meals per child; free meals reachable for a two-earner median family with two kids
policies.eligibility: All resident children; meal exemption by declaration to the institution.
policies.caveat: Bölcsőde coverage is patchy in small towns and villages (many have none), and waiting lists are common in Budapest; private crèches cost 150,000–250,000 HUF/month.
