policies.value: 100% of a ≈ 52,000 kr median monthly wage for 49 weeks shared (≈ 11 months), no cap bites at median wage
policies.eligibility: Worked with income in 6 of the last 10 months before leave; otherwise a one-off engangsstønad (≈ 92,000 kr, 2025).
policies.caveat: Quota weeks unused by one parent are lost; the 100%/80% choice cannot be changed later.

policies.name: Barnetrygd (child benefit)
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, monthly, automatic from birth to 18: 2,012 kr per child from 1 Feb 2026, now one flat rate for all ages (the previous higher under-6 rate and lower 6–18 rate were merged). Extra 512 kr in Finnmark/Svalbard; single parents get an extended benefit.
policies.value: 4,024 kr/month (≈ €345) for two children
policies.eligibility: Children resident in Norway; automatic for children born in Norway.

policies.name: Minstefradrag (standard wage deduction) + lower trygdeavgift
policies.what: Wage earners deduct 46% of wage income, up to 95,700 kr (2026), before the 22% ordinary income tax; the personfradrag of 114,540 kr (2026) is deducted on top. The employee social-security contribution (trygdeavgift) on wages has been cut stepwise from 8.2% (2022) to 7.6% (2026), with no contribution below 99,650 kr. Thresholds are adjusted yearly in the budget.
policies.value: ≈ 21,000 kr (≈ €1,800) less tax per earner from the minstefradrag at a 52,000 kr monthly wage (cap reached); ≈ 42,000 kr (≈ €3,600) per household; the trygdeavgift cut since 2022 saves a further ≈ 3,700 kr per earner
policies.eligibility: Automatic for everyone with wage income; no application.
policies.caveat: A flat deduction rather than a credit, so worth only 22% of its face value; trinnskatt (1.7–4.0% at median wage) and the 7.6% trygdeavgift still apply.

policies.name: Omsorgsdager / omsorgspenger (sick-child days)
policies.what: Each parent can stay home with full pay when a child under 12 is ill or the childminder is sick: 10 days per parent per year with 1–2 children (15 days with 3+; doubled for single parents), paid by the employer at ordinary salary up to 6G. Self-certification for the first 3 days.
policies.value: 20 paid days per year for the couple (≈ 1 month of salary protected)
policies.eligibility: Employees after 4 weeks in the job; self-employed from day 11.

policies.name: Arbeidsmiljøloven § 10-2: right to reduced and flexible working hours
policies.what: An employee with children under 10 (or other weighty welfare reasons) has a legal right to reduced working hours for a set period, unless this causes the employer a 'vesentlig ulempe' (substantial disadvantage); § 10-2(3) gives a parallel right to flexible hours. The employee keeps the right and duty to return to the original hours; disputes go to Tvisteløsningsnemnda.
policies.value: an enforceable right for either parent to work e.g. 80% until the youngest turns 10, with a guaranteed return to full time
policies.eligibility: All employees; parents of children under 10 are explicitly recognised as having a 'vektig grunn'.
policies.caveat: Without wage compensation; the employer can refuse on documented substantial-disadvantage grounds.

policies.name: Sykepenger 100% from day 1 + ferieloven 25 virkedager
policies.what: Illness: 100% of pay from the first sick day, the employer for the first 16 days, then Nav up to 6G (819,294 kr/year) for up to 52 weeks; self-certification (egenmelding) for short absences. Holiday: ferieloven gives 25 'virkedager' (4 weeks + 1 day, Saturdays count) with feriepenger of 10.2% of last year's wage; the 2000/01 wage settlement gives most employees a 5th week at 12%. ≈ 10 public holidays on top.
policies.value: no income loss at all when a parent is ill (median wage is below 6G); 4–5 weeks' holiday + ≈ 10 holidays per parent per year
policies.eligibility: Employees after 4 weeks of employment (sykepenger); holiday rights from day one, paid holiday from the second year.
policies.caveat: Feriepenger are earned the year before, so a first year in a new job means unpaid holiday; the 5th week is agreement-based.

policies.name: Free child healthcare, helsestasjon and public dental care
policies.what: Children under 16 pay no user fee (egenandel) at the GP, emergency room or hospital; the municipal helsestasjon provides free check-ups, home visit after birth and vaccinations to age 5; the public dental service treats children and young people free until 18 (reduced fee 19–24). School is free and 12 h/week of after-school SFO is free for 1st–2nd graders.
policies.value: ≈ 0 kr out of pocket for child health, dental and preventive care
policies.eligibility: All residents registered in the National Insurance Scheme.
policies.caveat: GP (fastlege) shortages in some municipalities; adults pay egenandel and full dental cost.

official.label: Nav — Familie (family benefits portal)

guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU/EEA social protection)

PL.note: Poland now front-loads cash on small children: universal 800+ plus the 2024 'Aktywny Rodzic' payment of 1,500 zł a month for every child aged 12–35 months make a two-toddler household one of the best-supported in the EU in pure cash terms. Paid leave is long (61 weeks, 81.5%) but the father's own 9 weeks are only 70%. Weak spots: nursery (żłobek) places for under-3s are still scarce outside big cities, and there is no housing support reachable at a median wage (the 2% first-home loan scheme closed in 2023; dodatek mieszkaniowy is for low incomes only). Labour taxation is middling for this household — the 2022 'Polski Ład' 30,000 zł tax-free amount and 12% rate help, but there is no earned-income credit, brackets have not moved since 2022 and the 9% health contribution is no longer deductible; the stronger side is work rights, where a parent can unilaterally reduce hours to half-time until the child's 6th year with dismissal protection, and paid leave plus 14 public holidays adds up to about 8 weeks off.

headline.cash: 1,600 zł/month (≈ €375) for 2 kids from 800+, plus 1,500 zł/month (≈ €350) per child aged 1–3 via Aktywny Rodzic
headline.leave: 20 weeks maternity + 41 weeks parental, 81.5% pay; 9 weeks reserved for the father at 70%; 2 weeks paternity at 100%
headline.childcare: public preschool from age 3: guaranteed place, 5 hours/day free; nursery fee covered up to 1,500 zł/month for ages 1–3
headline.tax: child tax credit 1,112 zł/year per child (≈ €520/year for 2), refundable; joint filing for spouses
headline.labourtax: no earned-income credit; 30,000 zł tax-free amount + 12% first rate since 2022 (≈ 3,600 zł/earner), brackets frozen since; 13.71% ZUS + 9% non-deductible health
headline.workrights: 20/26 days leave + 14 public holidays; parent of an under-6 can cut hours to 50% and employer must accept; no overtime without consent until child is 8

policies.name: Aktywny Rodzic (Active Parent) — 1,500 zł/month for children aged 12–35 months
policies.what: Since October 2024, for each child aged 12–35 months parents choose one of: 'Aktywni rodzice w pracy' 1,500 zł/month paid to working parents; 'Aktywnie w żłobku' up to 1,500 zł/month paid straight to the nursery/childminder (not above the actual fee); or 'Aktywnie w domu' 500 zł/month if the child stays home. No income ceiling.
policies.value: 1,500 zł/month (≈ €350) per child for 24 months — up to 36,000 zł per child; two toddlers can both qualify
policies.eligibility: Residents with a child aged 12–35 months. The 1,500 zł work variant requires both parents (or the sole parent) to be professionally active, roughly: social-insurance contributions from at least half the minimum wage each; the nursery variant only needs a place in a registered żłobek/klub/childminder.
policies.caveat: Replaced the old Rodzinny Kapitał Opiekuńczy (12,000 zł per second child) — households with only one child now get more than before. Nursery places remain scarce in many gminy, so the 1,500 zł 'in żłobek' option is often not usable in practice.

policies.name: Rodzina 800+ (świadczenie wychowawcze)
policies.what: Universal child benefit of 800 zł per month for every child until age 18 (raised from 500 zł in January 2024). No income test, paid by ZUS; benefit year runs June–May, application online each year.
policies.value: 1,600 zł/month (≈ €375) for 2 children, tax-free, on top of Aktywny Rodzic
policies.eligibility: All parents resident in Poland with children under 18; no income or work condition.
policies.caveat: Flat amount, not indexed — its real value erodes with inflation; the 2024 increase was the first since 2016.

policies.name: Paid maternity + parental leave (zasiłek macierzyński)
policies.what: 20 weeks maternity leave, then 41 weeks parental leave shared between parents, of which 9 weeks are non-transferable for each parent (since 2023). Benefit is 81.5% of pay for the whole 52 weeks (mother's share) if requested within 21 days of birth, otherwise 100% then 70%; the father's 9 reserved weeks are paid at 70%. Plus 2 weeks paternity leave at 100%.
policies.value: ≈ 5,100 zł/month (≈ €1,200) for about 12 months at a median wage (~7,300 zł gross), plus 9 weeks for the father at ~4,400 zł
policies.eligibility: Employees and other persons covered by sickness insurance (also self-employed paying contributions); no waiting period for employees.
policies.caveat: No cap for employees, but the 81.5% option must be requested in the first 21 days; the father's 9 weeks are lost if he does not take them.

policies.name: Kwota wolna 30,000 zł + 12% first PIT rate (Polski Ład, since 2022)
policies.what: Since 2022 the first 30,000 zł of annual income is tax-free (via a 3,600 zł 'kwota zmniejszająca podatek') and the first bracket up to 120,000 zł is taxed at 12% (17% before July 2022); 32% above. Applied monthly by the employer via PIT-2. Employee social contributions stay at 13.71% plus a 9% health contribution that is no longer deductible.
policies.value: 3,600 zł per earner, i.e. 7,200 zł/year (≈ €1,700) for two median earners; PIT on a ~7,300 zł gross wage is ≈ 5,100 zł/year (≈ 7% of gross)
policies.eligibility: Everyone taxed on the progressive scale (employment, civil-law contracts); both parents can use their own allowance, or file jointly.
policies.caveat: Neither the 30,000 zł allowance nor the 120,000 zł threshold is indexed, so real value erodes with wage growth; the 2023 election promise to raise the allowance to 60,000 zł has not been enacted. 'PIT-0' exemptions exist only for under-26s and 4+-child families.

policies.name: Ulga na dziecko (child tax credit) + joint spousal filing
policies.what: Annual income-tax credit of 1,112.04 zł for the first and second child each (2,000.04 zł third, 2,700 zł fourth+), deducted from PIT; any unused part is refunded up to the social/health contributions paid. With two or more children there is no income limit (112,000 zł joint limit applies only to one-child families). Spouses may also file jointly.
policies.value: 2,224 zł/year (≈ €520) for 2 children at a median wage; joint filing adds a further saving if one parent goes part-time
policies.eligibility: Parents taxed on the progressive scale (12%/32%); 2+ children: no income test.
policies.caveat: Amounts have been frozen since 2007 and are small relative to 800+; refund is limited to contributions actually paid.

policies.name: Right to cut working hours to 50% until the child's 6th year (art. 186⁷ KP) + flexible work until 8
policies.what: A parent entitled to urlop wychowawczy may instead ask to reduce hours to not less than half-time for the period the leave could be taken (up to 36 months, until the end of the calendar year in which the child turns 6) — the employer is obliged to grant it (21 days' notice). Dismissal is barred from the request until the end of the reduced hours, max 12 months. Parents of under-8s may also request flexible organisation (remote, flexitime, part-time; reasoned answer within 7 days) and cannot be given overtime, night work or travel without consent.
policies.value: e.g. a 4-day week (80%) for up to 36 months per child by right, with 12 months of dismissal protection; two paid 30-minute breastfeeding breaks a day
policies.eligibility: Employees with at least 6 months' employment history (for urlop wychowawczy) raising a child under 6; flexible-work request and overtime consent: any employee with a child under 8.
policies.url_label: gov.pl / MRPiPS — urlop wychowawczy: obniżenie wymiaru czasu pracy
policies.caveat: Pay falls in proportion; the flexible-work request (unlike the hours cut) can be refused with written reasons; the 12-month protection is shorter than the 36-month right.

policies.name: Paid annual leave 20/26 days + 14 public holidays; 80% sick pay from day 1; 60 days paid care for a sick child
policies.what: Statutory leave is 20 working days (26 after 10 years' 'employment history', into which a master's degree counts 8 years) plus 14 public holidays (Christmas Eve added in 2025). Own illness: employer pays 80% for the first 33 days a year, then ZUS zasiłek chorobowy at 80% (100% in pregnancy) up to 182 days. Sick child under 14: zasiłek opiekuńczy at 80% for up to 60 days a year per family, plus 2 days (16 h) a year of childcare leave at 100% and 5 days unpaid carer's leave.
policies.value: ≈ 26 days + 12 weekday holidays ≈ 7.5 weeks off at full pay for a 30-year-old graduate; a sick week for parent or child costs 20% of that week's pay
policies.eligibility: All employees on umowa o pracę; sickness and care benefits need sickness insurance (automatic for employees, 30-day waiting period at a new job).
policies.caveat: Two of the 14 holidays always fall on a Sunday; leave is pro-rated for the first job year; workers on civil-law contracts (zlecenie) have no annual leave and only voluntary sickness insurance.

policies.name: Public preschool (przedszkole) from age 3 — guaranteed place, 5 free hours
policies.what: Every child aged 3–6 has a legal right to a place in a public preschool run by its gmina; at least 5 hours a day are free, and each extra hour is capped by law (about 1.4 zł in 2025/26). Parents pay only for meals. The last year (age 6) is compulsory and free. Primary-school textbooks are free; child healthcare is free under NFZ.
policies.value: Full-day public preschool for roughly 150 zł/month in fees plus ~200–300 zł meals per child (≈ €80–110), vs 1,500–2,500 zł privately
policies.eligibility: All children resident in the gmina from the school year they turn 3 (2.5-year-olds if places allow).
policies.url_label: gov.pl / MEN — public preschool is free
policies.caveat: The guarantee starts at 3; for under-3s public żłobek coverage is still only around a third of children nationally and much lower in rural gminy.

official.label: Ministry of Family — family benefits portal (EN)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Poland

PT.note: For a young two-earner couple Portugal's big three are free crèche for every child born since Sept 2021 (Creche Feliz), the IRS Jovem tax exemption for workers up to 35, and solid parental leave paid at 100% (or 80–90% for longer options). Cash child benefit (abono de família) is income-tested and small at a median wage, and public pré-escolar is free from age 3. The catch is capacity: crèche and Porta 65 rent support are both rationed by places and rounds, and rents in Lisbon/Porto outrun any subsidy. Working parents also get some of the strongest legal conciliation rights in the EU (flexible hours or part-time as a right until the child is 12, telework until 3, 30 paid days a year for a sick child) and, beyond IRS Jovem, small yearly income-tax cuts, though the 11% employee contribution and a low median wage limit what any tax measure is worth in euros.

headline.cash: abono de família ≈ €90–220/month for 2 kids under 3 at a median household income (2026), falling after age 3
headline.leave: 120 days at 100% or 150 at 80% (150 at 100% / 180 at 83–90% if shared) + 28 days father-only at 100%
headline.childcare: Creche Feliz: free crèche 0–3 for all children born from 1 Sep 2021 (state pays €551.50/month); free public pré-escolar from 3
headline.tax: IRS Jovem: 100% income-tax exemption in year 1, 75% years 2–4, 50% years 5–7, 25% years 8–10, up to age 35 (cap €29,542/yr)
headline.labourtax: IRS Jovem up to 100% exemption to age 35; brackets indexed +3.51% and rates cut 0.3 pp for 2026; €4,587 work deduction; employee SS 11%
headline.workrights: 22 working days + 13 holidays + 13th/14th salary; legal right to flexible hours or part-time until child is 12; telework right until 3

policies.name: Creche Feliz — rede de creches gratuitas (free crèche 0–3)
policies.what: Every child born on or after 1 Sept 2021 gets a free place, regardless of family income, in crèches of the social/solidarity sector, licensed childminders and public or affiliated private crèches. The state pays the full base fee (€551.50/month in 2026) directly to the crèche. Fully phased in for all three crèche years since 2024/25.
policies.value: ≈ €550/month per child (≈ €13,000/yr for two children) versus paying privately
policies.eligibility: Children under 3 born from 1 Sept 2021; place must be requested online via Segurança Social Direta.
policies.url_label: Segurança Social — Creche Feliz, rede de creches gratuitas
policies.caveat: Free only where a place exists: waiting lists remain long in Lisbon, Porto and the Algarve, and non-affiliated private crèches are not covered. Meals/extended hours may still be charged.

policies.name: Licença parental inicial + licença parental exclusiva do pai
policies.what: Initial parental leave: 120 days at 100% of reference pay or 150 days at 80%; if the father takes at least 30 days alone, 150 days at 100% or 180 days at 83% (a 90% option for an equal split since 2023). Father: 28 days exclusive leave at 100% (7 right after birth) plus 7 optional; mother: 6 compulsory weeks.
policies.value: ≈ 5–6 months of full household pay replaced per birth, with no salary cap on the Social Security benefit
policies.eligibility: Employees and self-employed with 6 months of contributions; benefit paid by Segurança Social, tax-exempt.
policies.caveat: The additional 'licença parental alargada' (3 months per parent) is paid at only 25%. A citizens' bill for 180 days at 100% passed first reading in Jan 2026 but was not yet law in Sept 2026.

policies.name: IRS Jovem (young workers' income-tax exemption, 2025 model)
policies.what: Workers aged up to 35 pay reduced IRS on employment/self-employment income for 10 years: 100% exempt in year 1, 75% in years 2–4, 50% in years 5–7, 25% in years 8–10, on income up to 55× IAS (€29,542 in 2026). No degree required since 2025. Added to the standard child deduction of €600 per dependant (≈ €726–900 for under-3s).
policies.value: roughly €1,500–2,500/yr less tax per parent at a median wage in the 75% years; up to ≈ €5,000/yr for the household
policies.eligibility: Ages 18–35, not a dependant on someone else's return; opted in on the annual Modelo 3 (automatic proposal since 2026).
policies.url_label: Portal das Finanças — IRS Jovem FAQ
policies.caveat: Years used under the old (2020–24) regime count toward the 10; the benefit ends at 35 whatever remains.

policies.name: Horário flexível, tempo parcial e teletrabalho for parents (Código do Trabalho arts. 54–57 and 166)
policies.what: A parent of a child under 12 has the RIGHT to flexible hours or part-time work without career penalty; refusal requires a CITE opinion (30 days), rarely favourable. A parent of a child up to 3 may telework where the job allows (up to 8 if parents alternate, since 2023); two 1-hour feeding breaks daily until age 1.
policies.value: keeps two full-time wages while matching hours to crèche opening times; a 50% part-time year costs ≈ €9,500 of a €19,000 salary but the job and grade are protected
policies.eligibility: Employees with a child under 12 (flexible hours, part-time) or under 3 (telework); request in writing 30 days ahead; self-employed excluded.
policies.url_label: CITE — Direitos e deveres dos trabalhadores e das trabalhadoras (parentalidade)
policies.caveat: Flexible hours must still cover the employer's core period, and small firms can argue operational needs; telework rights depend on the job being remote-compatible.

policies.name: Férias, feriados, 13th/14th month, sick-child leave and tax-free meal allowance
policies.what: 22 working days paid leave + 13 national public holidays (+ municipal), plus mandatory holiday and Christmas bonuses of one month's pay each (14 salaries). Each parent may take 30 days a year for a sick child under 12, paid by Segurança Social at 65%. Meal allowances are tax- and contribution-free up to €6.15/day cash or €10.46/day by card (2026).
policies.value: ≈ 35 paid days off + 2 extra monthly salaries per earner; meal card worth ≈ €2,300/yr per earner tax-free where offered (most white-collar and public jobs)
policies.eligibility: All employees (Código do Trabalho); sick-child subsidy needs 6 months of contributions; meal allowance is set by employer or collective agreement, not statutory in the private sector.
policies.url_label: Portal das Finanças — Código do IRS (art. 2.º, exempt meal allowance limits)
policies.caveat: The 30 sick-child days are per parent but paid at only 65%; the meal allowance is not a legal right, and the 14th/13th salaries are already baked into the (low) annual median wage of roughly €19,000.

policies.name: IRS bracket indexation and rate cuts 2025–2026 (+ dedução específica)
policies.what: After across-the-board rate cuts in 2025, the 2026 State Budget raised all nine bracket limits by 3.51% and cut the rates of brackets 2–5 by 0.3 pp (12.5% up to €8,342; 15.7%; 21.2%; 24.1%; 31.1% up to €29,397). Every employee first deducts a 'dedução específica' of 8.54 × IAS ≈ €4,587 (2026); employee social security stays at 11%.
policies.value: roughly €100–150/yr less tax per earner at a €19,000 wage from the 2026 step alone (≈ €300–400/yr cumulative since 2024); mostly moot while IRS Jovem exempts 50–100% of the wage
policies.eligibility: Automatic for all resident taxpayers via withholding tables and the annual return.
policies.url_label: Portal das Finanças — Tabelas de retenção na fonte (IRS 2026)
policies.caveat: Indexation is decided each year in the budget, not automatic, and the 0.3 pp cuts are worth tens rather than hundreds of euros at a median wage; the 11% employee contribution is untouched.

policies.name: Abono de família para crianças e jovens
policies.what: Monthly child benefit by household reference income (annual income ÷ children+1). 2026 rates for a child under 3: €190.98 (1st bracket), €161.65 (2nd), €132.07 (3rd), €88.43 (4th); 4th bracket ends at €18,800 reference income. Children over 3 get €44.77–75.13; over 6 nothing in the 4th bracket. Extra for a second child under 3 (€39–65).
policies.value: roughly €90–220/month for a newborn + toddler (3rd–4th bracket at two median wages), dropping to ≈ €90 or less once both are over 3
policies.eligibility: Residents with children; reference income below ≈ €18,800/yr (2026); needs a yearly income re-check.
policies.caveat: Two full-time median earners sit near the top bracket and can lose the benefit entirely for children over 6; a birth grant (abono pré-natal) is paid only from the 13th week of pregnancy at the same bracket rates.

policies.name: Porta 65 Jovem (rent subsidy for under-35s)
policies.what: Pays a share of the rent to tenants aged 18–35 (one partner may be up to 37) for 12 months, renewable up to 5 years; average award ≈ €275/month in 2026. Household gross income must be below 4× the minimum wage (≈ €3,680/month in 2026) and rent below a municipal ceiling. Rolling online rounds on Portal da Habitação.
policies.value: ≈ €275/month (≈ €3,300/yr) if selected; two median earners with kids qualify on income
policies.eligibility: 18–35, renting a permanent home with a registered contract, no owned housing, income under the cap.
policies.caveat: Rounds are oversubscribed and ranked by lowest income, so median earners often miss out; rent ceilings are below market in Lisbon/Porto. Under-35 first-time buyers separately get IMT/stamp-duty exemption and a state mortgage guarantee, but only if they can afford the loan.

official.label: Segurança Social — family and parenthood benefits

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Portugal

RO.note: Romania's real strength for a two-earner family is time: an earnings-related child-raising benefit (85% of net pay) until the child is 2, on top of 126 days of maternity leave, and a cash bonus if a parent goes back to work early. Cash allowances are universal but have been frozen for two years (2025-2026) under austerity, a 10% health contribution has been taken from the child-raising benefit since Aug 2025, and there is no child tax relief at a median wage. Public kindergarten is free from age 3, but public creche places for under-3s are scarce and housing support is essentially absent. Romania takes 35% of gross pay in employee contributions plus a 10% flat tax with no relief reachable at a median wage, so the real perks of a job are in-kind: near-universal meal vouchers (up to 45 lei a day, free of the 25% pension contribution), 45 days a year of sick-child leave at 85% and four telework days a month for parents of children under 11.

headline.cash: ≈ 1,011 lei (≈ €200)/month for a newborn + toddler (alocația de stat, frozen 2025-2026)
headline.leave: 126 days maternity at 85% + child-raising leave to age 2 at 85% of net pay (min 1,651 / max 8,500 lei), 2 months reserved for the other parent; 10-15 days paternity
headline.childcare: public kindergarten free from age 3 (compulsory from 4); public creche free except meals (~13-22 lei/day) but places scarce
headline.tax: none reachable at median wage (personal deduction only up to ~6,050 lei gross)
headline.labourtax: flat 10% PIT + 35% employee contributions, no earned-income credit; basic deduction gone above ~6,300 lei gross; only 100 lei/month/child extra deduction
headline.workrights: 20 days paid leave + 17 public holidays; 4 telework days/month for parents of kids ≤11; 45 days/yr sick-child leave at 85%; meal vouchers 45 lei/day

policies.name: Indemnizația pentru creșterea copilului (child-raising leave and benefit)
policies.what: Either parent can stay home until the child turns 2 and receive 85% of their average net income of the previous 12 months, minimum 1,651 lei and maximum 8,500 lei gross per month (2026). At least 2 months are reserved for the other parent or are lost. Since 1 Aug 2025 a 10% health contribution (CASS) is deducted.
policies.value: ≈ 3,600-3,700 lei (≈ €710-730)/month net for up to 24 months per child for a parent on a median net wage of roughly 4,800 lei
policies.eligibility: 12 months of taxable income in the 2 years before the birth; one parent at a time; either parent.
policies.url_label: ANPIS (National Agency for Payments and Social Inspection) — Indemnizație creștere copil
policies.caveat: The 10% CASS deduction introduced by Law 141/2025 cuts the benefit by a tenth (max falls from 8,500 to 7,650 lei net). Payment starts only after the file is processed (often 1-3 months of delay).

policies.name: Alocația de stat pentru copii (universal child allowance)
policies.what: Monthly benefit for every child resident in Romania, no income test: 719 lei for children under 2 (under 3 if disabled) and 292 lei from age 2 to 18 (2026). The law provides automatic inflation indexation, but it was suspended for 2025 (OUG 156/2024) and again for 2026 (Law 141/2025).
policies.value: ≈ 1,011 lei (≈ €200)/month for a newborn (719) plus a 3-year-old (292)
policies.eligibility: All children legally resident in Romania; paid to the parent from the month after the application.
policies.url_label: ANPIS Bucharest — Alocație de stat pentru copii
policies.caveat: Frozen at Dec 2024 level for two consecutive years; real value has fallen roughly 10% with inflation. Drops from 719 to 292 lei on the child's 2nd birthday.

policies.name: Stimulentul de inserție (return-to-work bonus)
policies.what: A parent entitled to child-raising leave who instead earns taxable income gets a monthly bonus until the child is 2: 1,500 lei/month if they return before the child is 6 months old, 650 lei/month if they return later (2026). Paid on top of the salary; the other parent's leave months are not affected.
policies.value: 1,500 lei (≈ €295)/month for up to ~18 months if the second earner goes back before the baby is 6 months old; otherwise 650 lei (≈ €127)/month
policies.eligibility: Same 12-months-of-income condition as the child-raising benefit; must earn taxable income while receiving it.
policies.caveat: Cannot be combined with the child-raising benefit for the same parent; amounts are not indexed.

policies.name: Tichete de masă (meal vouchers, max 45 lei per working day)
policies.what: Employers may give an electronic meal card of up to 45 lei per day worked (2026 ceiling, up from 40.18 lei). The amount is subject to 10% income tax and 10% health contribution but exempt from the 25% pension contribution and the employer's 2.25% labour insurance; several million private and public employees receive it.
policies.value: ≈ 945 lei/month gross → ≈ 750 lei (≈ €150) net per earner, ≈ 18,000 lei (≈ €3,600)/year for two earners at the maximum; ≈ 25% more than the same sum paid as wages
policies.eligibility: Any employee whose employer chooses to grant vouchers; only for days actually worked (not during leave).
policies.url_label: ANAF — Codul fiscal (art. 76, 142: tax treatment of tichete de masă)
policies.caveat: Voluntary for the employer and capped per day; taxed 20% (PIT + CASS) since 2024; does not count toward pension.

policies.name: Concediu de maternitate + concediu paternal (maternity and paternity leave)
policies.what: Mothers get 126 calendar days of maternity leave (63 before + 63 after birth, minimum 42 days after birth) paid at 85% of the average income of the last 6 months from the health-insurance fund (CNAS), not the employer. Fathers get 10 working days of paid paternity leave, 15 days if they complete an infant-care course.
policies.value: ≈ 4 months at 85% of the mother's pay (≈ 4,100 lei ≈ €800/month at a 4,800 lei net wage) + 2-3 weeks fully paid for the father
policies.eligibility: Mother insured in the health system for at least 6 months in the last 12; father must be an employee.
policies.url_label: CNAS (National Health Insurance House) — maternity benefit payer
policies.caveat: The 85% is computed on income capped at 12 gross minimum wages; the maternity leave overlaps with the start of the child-raising leave rather than adding to it.

policies.name: Free public kindergarten from 3 and public creches; creche vouchers
policies.what: Public kindergarten (grădiniță) is free from age 3 and compulsory from age 4 (since 2023); parents of children in the extended day pay only a meal contribution of roughly 13-22 lei/day. Public creches (creșă, from 6 months) work the same way. Employers may give tax-free creche vouchers (up to 710 lei/month since Oct 2025) or reimburse creche/kindergarten fees up to 1,500 lei/month tax-free.
policies.value: ≈ 0 lei tuition for the 3-year-old; ~300-450 lei (≈ €60-90)/month for meals in a full-day public group
policies.eligibility: All resident children; enrolment via the national online platform each spring; priority to compulsory ages 4-5.
policies.caveat: Public creche capacity covers only a small share of under-3s, especially in Bucharest and big cities; private creches cost 2,000-4,000 lei/month. Creche vouchers exist only if the employer chooses to grant them and not while a parent is on child-raising leave.

policies.name: Concediu de odihnă, sărbători legale și telemuncă pentru părinți (leave, holidays, telework for parents)
policies.what: Labour Code: minimum 20 working days of paid annual leave (art. 145) plus 17 paid public holidays (art. 139). Since 2022 parents of children up to 11 can demand 4 days per month of work from home or telework (art. 118^1) and any employee can request an individualised/flexible schedule, which the employer must refuse in writing with reasons within 5 working days (art. 118).
policies.value: ≈ 37 paid days off per year per earner; up to 48 telework days per year for one parent (the other parent may not claim the same days)
policies.eligibility: All employees; telework days for a parent of a child up to 11 unless the nature of the job makes it impossible; both parents may not use the same days.
policies.url_label: Codul muncii PRO — art. 118^1 (telemuncă pentru părinți)
policies.caveat: No statutory right to reduce hours; telework can be refused where the job cannot be done remotely.

policies.name: Concediu pentru îngrijirea copilului bolnav + concediu medical (sick-child leave and own sick pay)
policies.what: Either insured parent may take up to 45 calendar days a year (more for serious illness, up to age 18) to care for a sick child under 7, paid at 85% of average income from the health fund (OUG 158/2005 art. 26-27). Own sickness: employer pays the first 5 calendar days; from 1 Aug 2025 the benefit is 55% (≤7 days), 65% (8-14 days) or 75% (15+ days) of the base.
policies.value: up to 45 days/year at ≈ 4,100 lei (≈ €800)/month equivalent for a parent on a 4,800 lei net wage; own sick pay cut to 55-75% since Aug 2025
policies.eligibility: 6 months of health contributions in the last 12; medical certificate; one parent at a time.
policies.caveat: Own-illness rates were cut in 2025 (55% for short episodes); sick-child days are per year, not per child.

policies.name: Deducere personală suplimentară pentru copii (extra tax deduction of 100 lei per child)
policies.what: Since 2023 one salaried parent may deduct 100 lei per month per child up to 18 enrolled in an education unit (creche, kindergarten or school) from taxable salary, regardless of wage level (Codul fiscal art. 77(10)(b)). The basic personal deduction only applies below minimum wage + 2,000 lei gross (≈ 6,300 lei in 2026), so a median earner gets none.
policies.value: ≈ 10 lei/month per child in tax saved → 240 lei (≈ €48)/year for two enrolled children; the basic deduction is worth 0 at a median wage
policies.eligibility: Parent with salary income; child enrolled in an education unit; only one parent, one employer; enrolment certificate + declaration.
policies.caveat: Tiny: a 10% flat tax on a 100 lei deduction; nothing for a baby not yet in creche; no relief from the 35% employee contributions.

official.label: ANPIS — family benefits agency (site frequently returns 503 to non-Romanian traffic)

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Romania

SE.note: Sweden's package for a two-earner couple with small children rests on long, well-paid parental leave (480 days per child, ~80% of wage), near-free förskola under the maxtaxa (cut again from July 2026) and generous paid sick-child days. The universal child benefit has been frozen at 1,250 kr since 2018 and the housing allowance is unreachable at two median wages; Sweden has no family taxation. The real weak spot for renters is the housing market itself: first-hand rental queues in Stockholm and Gothenburg run many years. Sweden taxes wages at ≈ 32% municipal rate but has no employee social contributions and a large earned-income credit (roughly 4,000 kr/month per median earner in 2026), and its parental-leave law gives a hard legal right to a 75% schedule until the child is 8 plus a right to request flexible work.

headline.cash: 2,650 kr/month (≈ €240) tax-free barnbidrag + flerbarnstillägg for 2 children (frozen since 2018)
headline.leave: 480 days per child, 390 at ~80% of wage (max 1,259 kr/day 2026), 90 days reserved per parent; + 120 sick-child days/child/year at ~80%
headline.childcare: place guaranteed from age 1; max 1,547 kr/month child 1 + 1,031 kr child 2 from 1 July 2026, meals included; 15 h/week free from age 3
headline.tax: none: individual taxation, no child tax credit
headline.labourtax: jobbskatteavdrag (earned-income credit) enlarged again for 2026: roughly 4,000 kr/month per median earner; individual taxation, no employee social contributions
headline.workrights: 25 days paid leave + ≈ 12 public holidays; legal right to cut hours by 25% until child is 8; employer sick pay 80% days 2–14

policies.name: Föräldrapenning (parental benefit)
policies.what: 480 days per child: 390 at just under 80% of income, max 1,259 kr/day in 2026 (income ceiling 592,000 kr/year), plus 90 days at 180 kr/day. 90 days reserved for each parent; up to 45 days can go to e.g. a grandparent (since July 2024). Usable until age 12; 60 double days before 15 months; other parent gets 10 paid days at birth.
policies.value: ≈ 29,000 kr/month (≈ €2,650) before tax at a 38,000 kr median wage, for ≈ 13 months at the high rate per child; many employers add föräldralön to ~90%
policies.eligibility: Insured in Sweden; income-based rate needs 240 days of SGI before birth, otherwise 250 kr/day basic level.
policies.caveat: Only 96 days can be saved past age 4; the 180 kr lowest-level days are close to worthless.

policies.name: Förskola under the maxtaxa (fee cap)
policies.what: Municipalities must offer a förskola place within 4 months of application from age 1, full-day with meals. National fee cap from 1 July 2026: first 10,000 kr of monthly household income exempt, then 3% for child 1 (max 1,547 kr), 2% for child 2 (max 1,031 kr), 1% for child 3 (max 516 kr), ceiling income 61,560 kr/month. 15 h/week free from age 3.
policies.value: ≈ 2,580 kr/month (≈ €235) for two full-time places incl. meals at two median wages (≈ 3,080 kr before July 2026)
policies.eligibility: All children from age 1 whose parents work, study, are on parental leave (limited hours) or unemployed.
policies.url_label: Stockholm stad — förskola fees 2026 (national maxtaxa rates)
policies.caveat: Place may be offered anywhere in the municipality; queues for specific popular förskolor; some big cities have staffing shortages.

policies.name: Jobbskatteavdrag (earned-income tax credit, 67 kap. 7 § inkomstskattelagen)
policies.what: A credit against income tax on wages only, computed from prisbasbelopp bands and the municipal tax rate; enlarged in the 2025 and again in the 2026 budget (Lag 2025:1376: bands 0.91/3.24/8.08 prisbasbelopp, 38.74% and 25.1% marginal build-up, max 3.027 prisbasbelopp minus grundavdrag). Applied automatically via the tax table; no application.
policies.value: roughly 50,000 kr/year (≈ 4,000 kr/month, ≈ €360) per earner at a 38,000 kr monthly wage in 2026 by own calculation from the statutory formula (prisbasbelopp ≈ 59,200 kr, municipal tax ≈ 32.4%); ≈ 100,000 kr/year (≈ €9,000) per household
policies.eligibility: Everyone under 66 with Swedish-taxed wage or business income; a separate, smaller formula applies from age 66.
policies.caveat: The exact amount depends on the municipal tax rate (29–35%) and is our own computation from the 2026 formula; the credit is per person and does not vary with children.

policies.name: Tillfällig föräldrapenning / VAB (care of sick child)
policies.what: When a child under 12 is ill, either parent can stay home and claim VAB: up to 120 days per child per year at just under 80% of income (income cap 444,000 kr/year in 2026, i.e. roughly 940 kr/day max). Claimed online the same day; no doctor's note for the first 7 days.
policies.value: ≈ 900 kr/day (≈ €80) per sick day; a family with two toddlers in förskola typically uses 15–25 days a year (≈ 15,000–22,000 kr)
policies.eligibility: Working parents (or others caring for the child) with SGI in Sweden.
policies.url_label: Försäkringskassan — Care of a sick child (VAB)

policies.name: Barnbidrag + flerbarnstillägg (child benefit)
policies.what: Universal, tax-free, paid monthly and split between parents: 1,250 kr per child under 16 plus a large-family supplement of 150 kr for the second child (730 kr for three). Automatic, no application. The 1,250 kr rate has not been raised since March 2018.
policies.value: 2,650 kr/month (≈ €240) for two children
policies.eligibility: All children resident and insured in Sweden.
policies.caveat: Frozen in nominal terms since 2018, so its real value has fallen by roughly a quarter.

policies.name: Föräldraledighetslagen: right to 75% hours until age 8 + flexible-work request
policies.what: 7 §: a parent may cut normal working time by up to a quarter (to 75%) to care for a child under 8 or not yet through the first school year (second school year from 1 July 2028), without using parental benefit; 15a–c §§ (since Aug 2022): parents of children under 8 may request remote work or flexible hours and the employer must answer with reasons. Leave can be split into 3 periods a year; dismissal or worse treatment for using these rights is unlawful (16–17 §§).
policies.value: an enforceable right for both parents to work 30 h/week (at 75% pay) for ≈ 8 years, plus job protection on return from leave
policies.eligibility: All employees; part-time right needs 6 months' service (or 12 months in the last 2 years) and 2 months' notice.
policies.caveat: Reduced hours mean reduced pay; the flexible-work request can be refused with a written reason.

policies.name: Semesterlagen 25 days + employer sjuklön 80%
policies.what: Semesterlagen: 25 paid holiday days a year for every employee (many agreements 28–30), with semesterlön ≈ 12% or pay + 0.43% per day, plus ≈ 12 public holidays. Own illness: the employer pays sjuklön at 80% for days 1–14 after a karensavdrag of 20% of a week's sjuklön; from day 15 Försäkringskassan pays sjukpenning at ≈ 77.6% up to 10 prisbasbelopp (≈ 592,000 kr/year in 2026), which fully covers a median wage.
policies.value: 25 paid days + ≈ 12 holidays per parent; ≈ 80% of pay from day 2 of any illness, no medical certificate needed for the first 7 days
policies.eligibility: All employees; sjuklön from the first day of employment (agreed employment of at least 1 month or 14 days worked).
policies.caveat: Holiday in the first year may be unpaid unless earned; the karensavdrag costs ≈ one day's pay per sick spell.

policies.name: Free child healthcare, BVC and dental care
policies.what: Children pay no fee for outpatient care in most regions (usually to age 18–20), prescription medicines are free under 18, and the child health centre (BVC) provides free check-ups, vaccinations and home visits. Dental care is free through the year the person turns 19 (lowered from 23 on 1 Jan 2025). School meals are free from förskoleklass.
policies.value: ≈ 0 kr out of pocket for child health and dental
policies.eligibility: All children registered in a region.
policies.caveat: Age limits for free care differ by region; the free-dental age was cut from 23 to 19 in 2025.

official.label: Försäkringskassan — Parents (English)

guide.label: MISSOC comparative tables (EU/EEA social protection)

SI.note: Slovenia is among the most generous countries in Europe for a working couple with babies: roughly a year of leave at 100% pay per child (maternity uncapped, parental capped at 2.5x the average wage), 15 days of paid paternity, and a second child in public kindergarten for free. Child benefit and kindergarten fees are income-graded, so at two median wages the family still pays a substantial fee for the first child and gets only a small child allowance, but the child tax relief is real. Rent subsidies are targeted at low incomes; free school lunches for all arrive only in September 2027. Slovenia also pays its workers a lot outside the taxed wage: a statutory holiday allowance of at least the minimum wage, a new winter allowance of half the minimum wage from 2025, and daily meal and commuting money, all free of tax and contributions, while a parent has a legal right to work half-time until the child is 3 (until the younger child is 8 with two children) with the state covering the missing social contributions.

headline.cash: ≈ €89/month child benefit for 2 kids at ~€725 net per family member (up to €340 for low incomes); €441.60 birth grant
headline.leave: 105 days maternity at 100% + 160 days parental per parent (60 non-transferable) at 100%, cap €6,340/month; 15 days paternity at 100%
headline.childcare: public kindergarten from 11 months, fee 0-77% of price by income; second child attending at the same time is free
headline.tax: €6,252.60/year off taxable income for 2 children (2026) → ≈ €1,600/year less income tax
headline.labourtax: statutory regres (≥ min wage) + new winter regres (½ min wage) + meal/commute allowances all tax- and contribution-free; scale and allowances indexed (+5.5% in 2026)
headline.workrights: 4 weeks leave + 1 day per child + 13 holidays; right to work 20-40h/week until the child is 3 (8 with two kids) with the state paying contributions

policies.name: Materinski, očetovski in starševski dopust (maternity, paternity and parental leave)
policies.what: Maternity leave of 105 days (starting 28 days before birth) at 100% of the average wage of the last 12 months, uncapped. Then parental leave of 160 calendar days for each parent, 60 of them non-transferable (raised from 30 on 1 June 2026), 100 transferable, at 100% of the base capped at 2.5x the average gross wage (≈ €6,340/month in 2026). Fathers also get 15 days of paternity leave at 100% before the child is 3 months old.
policies.value: ≈ 12 months of full net pay for the mother (105 + 260 days) plus 15 + 60 days for the father per child at a median net wage of ~€1,450; can be split more evenly
policies.eligibility: Parent insured for parental protection (all employees and self-employed); uninsured parents get a flat €402 parental supplement instead.
policies.caveat: Base is limited to 2.5x the average wage; the father's 60 non-transferable days expire if unused (until the child is 8). Parental leave can be taken part-time until age 8 but the days are then used up faster.

policies.name: Znižano plačilo vrtca (income-graded public kindergarten fee, second child free)
policies.what: Public kindergartens accept children from 11 months. Parents pay 0-77% of the programme price depending on income class per family member (9 classes; the top class pays 77%); municipalities pay the rest. If two children attend at the same time the younger one is free (paid by the state); the 3rd and further children are free regardless. Applied for at the Centre for Social Work (CSD).
policies.value: ≈ €250-300/month for the first child (43% of a ~€600-650 first-age-group price at ~€725 net per family member), €0 for the second child attending simultaneously
policies.eligibility: All resident children; fee class set by CSD on last year's net income and assets; without an application the full 77% is charged.
policies.url_label: gov.si — Vpis v vrtec in plačilo vrtca
policies.caveat: Enrolment coverage is high (~85% of 1-5-year-olds) but Ljubljana and its suburbs run waiting lists for under-2s; price and the municipal share vary by municipality.

policies.name: Neobdavčeni regres, zimski regres, malica in prevoz (tax-free statutory holiday, winter, meal and commuting allowances)
policies.what: Every employer must pay a holiday allowance (regres) of at least the minimum wage (€1,277.72 in 2025, indexed each January) by 1 July (ZDR-1 art. 131), a winter allowance of half the minimum wage (€638.86 for 2025) by 18 December under the 2025 ZPZR act, and reimburse meals during work (€7.96 per day tax-free) and commuting (€0.21/km or the bus pass) (art. 130). All are exempt from income tax and social contributions up to those limits.
policies.value: ≈ €1,300 + €640 + ≈ €1,750 meal money ≈ €3,700 per earner per year received net of tax; ≈ €7,400 for two earners, worth roughly €1,500 per earner more than the same money paid as taxable wage
policies.eligibility: All employees with a right to annual leave; pro rata for part-time or part-year employment; meal money for days worked.
policies.url_label: FURS — dohodek iz zaposlitve (regres, zimski regres, povračila stroškov)
policies.caveat: Regres above the average wage and winter regres plus performance bonus above the average wage become taxable; employers in difficulty may pay the winter allowance as late as 31 March.

policies.name: Posebna olajšava za vzdrževane otroke (child tax relief)
policies.what: Annual income-tax relief deducted from taxable income: €2,995.83 for the 1st child, €3,256.77 for the 2nd, €5,432.02 for the 3rd, rising by €2,060.97 for each further child (2026 tax year; 2025: €2,838.30 / €3,085.52). Claimed monthly via the employer or by an application to FURS by early February; parents may split children between them.
policies.value: ≈ €6,252.60/year off taxable income for 2 children → roughly €1,600/year (≈ €135/month) less tax at the 26% bracket
policies.eligibility: Resident taxpayer supporting a child under 18 (or in education up to 26).
policies.url_label: eUprava — Olajšava za vzdrževane družinske člane
policies.caveat: Worth more to the higher earner; a parent with very low taxable income cannot use it fully. Deadline for the annual application is 5 Feb (paper) / 20 Feb (eDavki).

policies.name: Krajši delovni čas zaradi starševstva (right to part-time work for parents, state-paid contributions)
policies.what: One parent (or both, sharing) has a legal right to work part-time — at least 20 hours a week — until the child turns 3, or until the younger child turns 8 when caring for two or more children (ZSDP-1). The employer pays the hours worked; the state pays the social security contributions for the unworked hours on a base of at least the proportional minimum wage, so pension and health cover stay full.
policies.value: e.g. 30 h/week instead of 40 until the second child is 8: the parent gives up ≈ 25% of net pay (≈ €360/month at a €1,450 median net wage) but keeps full social insurance; both parents may split the 20 missing hours
policies.eligibility: Employed or self-employed parents insured for parental protection; apply at the social work centre within 30 days of starting part-time; child under 3 (or youngest under 8 with 2+ children).
policies.url_label: eUprava — krajši delovni čas zaradi starševstva
policies.caveat: The lost hours are unpaid; the state only covers contributions, and regres is paid pro rata unless the reduction is under this right.

policies.name: Otroški dodatek (means-tested child benefit)
policies.what: Monthly benefit for children up to 18, graded in 8 income classes by net income per family member up to €1,328.28 (from 1 March 2026, indexed 2.7%). Class 1 (≤ €241.49/member) gets €147.69 for a 1st and €162.45 for a 2nd child; class 6 (€711.12-858.67) €39.32 + €49.21; class 8 (€1,100.20-1,328.28) €25.70 + €35.53. +20% for a child under 4 not in kindergarten, +30% in single-parent families.
policies.value: ≈ €89/month for 2 children at ~€725 net per family member (class 6), up to ≈ €106 if the baby is not in kindergarten; €310 for a low-income family
policies.eligibility: Resident families under the income ceiling; one application at the CSD, renewed yearly.
policies.caveat: Amounts fall steeply with income; a couple both above the median wage may be in class 7-8 and receive under €70 for two children.

policies.name: Pomoč ob rojstvu otroka (universal birth grant)
policies.what: One-off payment of €441.60 per newborn (from 1 March 2026; €429.99 before) with no income test, applied for at the CSD before the child is 60 days old. Many municipalities add their own newborn grant (roughly €100-500). Children's healthcare is free and primary-school textbooks are lent free from the school textbook fund; school lunch becomes free for all pupils from 1 Sept 2027.
policies.value: €883.20 from the state for two births, plus a municipal grant in most municipalities
policies.eligibility: Resident parent; application within 60 days of birth.
policies.url_label: eUprava — Vodič: postopki ob rojstvu otroka
policies.caveat: Rent subsidy (subvencija najemnine) exists but is calculated around the minimum-income level (€507.43 basic amount in 2026) and priority lists for non-profit housing, so it does not reach a two-median-wage household.

policies.name: Letni dopust, prazniki in nega otroka (annual leave with child bonus days, holidays, sick-child care)
policies.what: ZDR-1: at least 4 weeks of paid leave plus 1 extra day for each child under 15 (art. 159), on top of 13 work-free public holidays. Care of a sick child under 7 is paid at 80% of the base by the health insurer ZZZS from day 1 for up to 15 working days per episode (7 days for older children, extendable). A breastfeeding mother working full time gets a paid 1-hour break per day until the child is 18 months.
policies.value: ≈ 22 leave days + 13 holidays per earner per year with two children; sick-child care at ≈ €1,160/month equivalent (80% of a €1,450 net wage)
policies.eligibility: All employees; extra days per child under 15; sick-child care for insured parents with a doctor's note.
policies.url_label: Uradni list RS — Zakon o delovnih razmerjih (ZDR-1), čl. 130-131, 159
policies.caveat: Own sickness is paid by the employer at 80% for the first 30 working days (90% for injury at work), then by ZZZS.

policies.name: Uskladitev dohodninske lestvice in olajšav (annual indexation of tax brackets and allowances)
policies.what: Tax brackets, the general allowance and child reliefs are adjusted every year by regulation: for 2026 they rose 5.5% (general allowance €5,551.93 vs €5,260 in 2025; 16% bracket up to €9,721.43; 1st child relief €2,995.83). Employees up to age 29 additionally get a €1,443.50 youth allowance (2026), which parents of 30 have just outgrown.
policies.value: roughly €120-150/year less tax per earner in 2026 from indexation alone at a ≈ €2,150 gross median wage; the youth allowance would be worth ≈ €375/year but stops after age 29
policies.eligibility: Automatic for all taxpayers; youth allowance only for employees up to 29, pro rata by months worked.
policies.url_label: FURS — lestvica za odmero dohodnine in olajšave 2026
policies.caveat: Indexation only stops fiscal drag; employee contributions stay at 22.1% of gross with no relief.

guide.label: European Commission — Your social security rights in Slovenia

SK.note: Slovakia's strongest instruments are the tax-free maternity benefit (75% of pay for 34 weeks, and up to 28 weeks for the father too) and a parental allowance of €500 a month until the child is 3 that the parent may keep while working full-time. The €60 child allowance is small and frozen, and the €100/month child tax bonus was trimmed in the 2025 consolidation package. Kindergarten places are now a legal right from age 3 and cheap, but public care for under-3s barely exists, and there is no housing help reachable at a median wage. Labour taxation offers little beyond the child bonus — a €5,967 tax-free allowance that is at least indexed each year, 19% PIT and 13.4% contributions with no parent-specific cuts — but work rights are unusually parent-friendly: five weeks' paid leave for any employee raising a child, a mandatory tax-free employer meal contribution worth about €1,100 a year per earner, a €275 recreation allowance in larger firms, and a claim to shorter hours until the child is 15.

headline.cash: €500.10/month parental allowance until age 3 (paid even if the parent works) + €60/month child allowance per child + €829.86 birth grant
headline.leave: 34 weeks maternity at 75% (tax-free, cap €2,330/month); father: 2 weeks paternity + up to 26 further weeks of maternity benefit before age 3
headline.childcare: legal right to a public kindergarten place from age 3 (since 2025/26); municipal fee typically €20–60/month; free from age 5
headline.tax: child tax bonus €100/month per child under 15 (€200/month for two), phased out only above ~€2,300 gross/month
headline.labourtax: 19% PIT above a €5,966.73 allowance (2026, indexed yearly to the subsistence minimum); 13.4% employee contributions; no earned-income credit beyond the child bonus
headline.workrights: 5 weeks paid leave for anyone raising a child + 14 holidays; mandatory employer meal contribution (€5.12/shift tax-free); part-time on request until child is 15

policies.name: Materské (maternity benefit) incl. father's share + otcovské
policies.what: Sickness-insurance benefit of 75% of the daily assessment base, tax-free, for 34 weeks (37 single parent, 43 for twins), starting 6–8 weeks before birth; cap €2,329.90 per 31-day month in 2026. The father can take 2 weeks 'otcovské' in the first 6 weeks and, separately, up to 26 further weeks of materské any time before the child turns 3 (while the mother is not drawing it). From April 2026 paid automatically without a formal application.
policies.value: ≈ €1,125/month tax-free for 8 months at a median wage (~€1,500 gross), plus ≈ €1,125/month for up to 28 weeks if the father takes his part
policies.eligibility: 270 days of sickness insurance in the last 2 years (employees are insured automatically; self-employed if paying contributions).
policies.caveat: The father's 26 weeks require him to stop working for that employer during the leave (he may work elsewhere); both parents cannot draw for the same child at the same time.

policies.name: Rodičovský príspevok (parental allowance) until age 3
policies.what: Flat monthly state allowance for the parent caring for a child under 3: €500.10 in 2026 if that parent had drawn maternity benefit, €364.80 otherwise; indexed each January. Paid regardless of income and even if the parent returns to full-time work and the child attends nursery. One allowance per family (higher for multiples).
policies.value: €500.10/month, i.e. ≈ €6,000/year, for a family with a child under 3 — with two children born ~2 years apart, roughly 5 years of continuous payments
policies.eligibility: Parent with permanent/temporary residence caring for a child under 3 (under 6 with long-term illness); no work or income condition.
policies.caveat: Cannot be combined with materské in the same month; the lower €364.80 rate applies to parents who never qualified for maternity benefit.

policies.name: Daňový bonus na dieťa (child tax bonus)
policies.what: Monthly reduction of income tax of €100 per child under 15 and €50 for ages 15–17 (2026), applied by the employer; refundable as a payment if tax is too low. Capped at a percentage of the tax base (29% for one child, 36% for two) — partners may add their bases together. Since 2025 it is reduced by 1/10 of income above 1.5× the average wage (~€2,290 gross/month).
policies.value: €200/month (≈ €2,400/year) for two children under 15 at a median wage
policies.eligibility: Parents with earned income (employment or business); child under 18; full amount up to ~€2,290 gross/month, phased out above.
policies.caveat: Cut in the 2025 consolidation package: bonus for children 18+ abolished and the high-income phase-out introduced; a parent on parental leave with no earnings cannot claim it alone.

policies.name: Nezdaniteľná časť základu dane — €5,966.73 tax-free allowance (2026), indexed to the subsistence minimum
policies.what: Each taxpayer's first €5,966.73 of annual tax base is untaxed in 2026 (21× the subsistence minimum of €284.13; €5,753.79 in 2025), applied monthly by the employer (€497.23/month). The allowance rises automatically every year with the subsistence minimum, so the 19%/25% brackets are partly protected from fiscal drag. Employee contributions are 13.4% (9.4% social + 4% health) with no reduction for parents.
policies.value: ≈ €1,134/year per earner (19% × €5,966.73), ≈ €2,270 per household of two median earners (~€1,500 gross/month each)
policies.eligibility: All resident taxpayers with a tax base up to 92.8× the subsistence minimum (≈ €26,370 in 2026); phased out above.
policies.url_label: Finančná správa — zamestnanci: daň z príjmov (nezdaniteľná časť 2026)
policies.caveat: No earned-income or work-bonus credit exists; the tax exemptions for 13th/14th salaries were abolished in 2021, and the 2025 consolidation package raised health contributions (employer side) rather than cutting labour taxes.

policies.name: Prídavok na dieťa (child allowance) + príspevok pri narodení (birth grant)
policies.what: Universal child allowance of €60 per month per child until the end of full-time education (max age 25), plus a one-off €110 in the month the child starts first grade. Separately, a birth grant of €829.86 for each of the first three children (2026), paid to the mother.
policies.value: €120/month (≈ €1,440/year) for two children, plus €829.86 per birth
policies.eligibility: All residents with dependent children; no income test.
policies.caveat: Frozen at €60 since 2023 and not indexed — one of the lowest child allowances in the EU relative to wages.

policies.name: 5 weeks' paid leave for any employee raising a child (§ 103 ZP) + 14 paid public holidays
policies.what: Basic leave is 4 weeks, but an employee who permanently cares for a child gets at least 5 weeks regardless of age (since 2020; otherwise only from age 33). Slovakia has 15 public holidays, of which 1 September has been a working day since 2025 — 14 paid days off. Own illness: employer pays 25% (days 1–3) and 55% (days 4–10), then Sociálna poisťovňa nemocenské at 55%; sick child under 11: ošetrovné at 55% for up to 14 days per case, and 'dlhodobé ošetrovné' at 55% for up to 90 days.
policies.value: 5 weeks + ~10 weekday holidays ≈ 7 weeks off at full pay per parent from the first child onward
policies.eligibility: All employees with an employment contract; the 5th week is claimed by declaring you care for a child (no age limit stated in the law).
policies.caveat: Sick pay is among the lowest in the EU (25%/55%); ošetrovné needs a doctor's certificate and is paid per illness, not per year; a second public holiday was debated for removal in the 2026 consolidation round.

policies.name: Mandatory employer meal contribution (stravné) — €5.12/shift tax-free from Dec 2025 + €275 recreation allowance
policies.what: Every employer must provide a meal, a meal voucher or a cash meal allowance for each shift over 4 hours; the employer pays at least 55% of the meal price, tax- and contribution-free up to 55% of the €9.30 business-trip meal rate — €5.12 per shift from 1 December 2025 (voucher value at least €6.98). Separately, employers with more than 49 staff must reimburse 55% of a domestic holiday, up to €275 a year, tax-free (rekreačný poukaz, § 152a) for employees with 24 months' service.
policies.value: ≈ €1,150/year per earner tax-free (225 shifts × €5.12), ≈ €2,300 per household, plus up to €550 for two recreation allowances in larger firms
policies.eligibility: All employees working shifts over 4 hours (employer's choice of form); recreation allowance: employers with 50+ employees, ≥ 24 months' tenure, on request with receipts.
policies.url_label: Finančná správa (podpora) — stravovanie zamestnancov v roku 2026
policies.caveat: Employers may pay only the 55% minimum of a cheaper meal; the recreation allowance is voluntary for firms under 50 staff and needs the employee to pay 45% of the holiday first.

policies.name: Shorter hours or adjusted schedule on request until the child is 15 (§ 164 ZP) + home-office request until 8
policies.what: A pregnant employee or a parent permanently caring for a child under 15 who asks for shorter working time or another suitable arrangement must be granted it unless serious operational reasons prevent it. A parent of a child under 3 may not be ordered to work overtime or on-call. Since November 2022 parents of children under 8 may request home office or other flexible work and the employer must refuse in writing with reasons. After maternity/parental leave the employee returns to the same job (or an equivalent one at the same pay).
policies.value: e.g. a 30-hour week or fixed early shifts by right until the youngest child is 15; no compulsory overtime while a child is under 3
policies.eligibility: All employees; the request is made in writing and can be time-limited.
policies.url_label: MPSVR SR — Zákonník práce (overview and text)
policies.caveat: 'Serious operational reasons' is undefined and rarely litigated; flexible work is a right to a reasoned answer only; pay falls with hours and the €500 parental allowance is the only cushion.

policies.name: Materská škola (public kindergarten) — legal right to a place from age 3
policies.what: From school year 2025/26 every child who turns 3 by 31 August has a legal right to a place in the catchment municipal kindergarten (another municipal one if full). Fees are set by the municipality — typically €20–60 per month plus meals — and the compulsory final year (from age 5) is free in public kindergartens.
policies.value: Full-day public kindergarten for roughly €60–120/month per child including meals (≈ 5% of a median wage); free in the last year
policies.eligibility: All children resident in the municipality from age 3 (younger only if capacity allows).
policies.caveat: Public nurseries (jasle) for under-3s are almost non-existent; private nursery costs €400–800/month and the alternative 'príspevok na starostlivosť o dieťa' (max €280) is worth less than the €500 parental allowance.
